item.title: South African rand holds near multi-month high as Iran sanctions loom
item.description: The South African rand opened the week on a firm footing on Monday, hovering near its strongest level since the start of the Iran war, as a subdued dollar, higher gold prices and strength across emerging-market currencies supported the commodity-linked currency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The South African rand opened the week on a firm footing on Monday, hovering near its strongest level since the start of the Iran war , as a subdued dollar, higher gold prices and strength across emerging-market currencies supported the commodity-linked currency. At 0636 GMT, the rand traded at 15.99 against the dollar , up about 0.2% and not far from its strongest level since the start of the Iran war touched earlier in the session. South Africa's key export, gold, hit its [USN:L1N44L03D TEXT:"highest level in more than three months"] as a subdued dollar lent support, while investors looked ahead to key U.S. inflation data and a speech by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh later this week. The dollar was [USN:L1N44L061 TEXT:"pinned near multi-month lows"] as traders awaited details of a fresh U.S. sanctions package against Iran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1800 GMT after threatening "[USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"the toughest sanctions in history"]" on Iran, while Iran's foreign minister [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"dismissed"] the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation. Wichard Cilliers, head of market risk at TreasuryONE, said the rand's rally was being driven by broad dollar weakness, strong emerging-market sentiment and higher gold prices. Like other risk-sensitive currencies, the rand has been at the mercy of global market sentiment, particularly since the start of the U.S.-Iran war on February 28. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was slightly firmer in early deals, as the yield fell 1.5 basis points to 8.565%.

item.title: Thames Water's creditors line up new board under proposed rescue deal
item.description: A group of senior creditors of struggling British utility Thames Water said on Monday it had picked an initial cohort of directors to lead the debt-laden company if its rescue deal goes through.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A group of senior creditors of struggling British utility Thames Water said on Monday it had picked an initial cohort of directors to lead the debt-laden company if its rescue deal goes through. Mike McTighe, Liz Barber, Clive Selley and Bernadette Kelly are among the proposed non-executive directors for the Thames Water board, the London & Valley Water consortium said. "It is proposed that these individuals will join the Thames Water board to oversee Thames Water's 10-year turnaround and deliver a comprehensive transformation of Thames Water in the interest of customers and the public," the consortium said.

item.title: La UE aprueba una nueva ayuda de 6.100 millones de euros para la defensa de Ucrania
item.description: La Comisión Europea aprobó el lunes una nueva ayuda financiera de 6.100 millones de euros (7.120 millones de dólares) para Ucrania, destinada a la adquisición de nuevos sistemas de defensa, como sistemas de defensa aérea, misiles, munición y radares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Comisión Europea aprobó el lunes una nueva ayuda financiera de 6.100 millones de euros (7.120 millones de dólares) para Ucrania, destinada a la adquisición de nuevos sistemas de defensa, como sistemas de defensa aérea, misiles, munición y radares. La UE señaló que este nuevo paquete de ayuda se suma a los 16.000 millones de euros de planes de adquisición aprobados anteriormente, de los cuales ya se habían desembolsado 8.350 millones de euros. "A medida que Rusia intensifica sus ataques, redoblamos nuestros esfuerzos para ayudar a Ucrania a proteger a su población y defender su espacio aéreo. Europa está del lado de Ucrania y le proporcionaremos lo que necesite, cuando lo necesite", afirmó la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, en un comunicado. item.title: Report: 49ers trade RB Zamir White to Saints for LB Deion Jones
item.description: The New Orleans Saints are acquiring running back Zamir White from the San Francsico 49ers for linebacker Deion Jones, ESPN reported late Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New Orleans Saints are acquiring running back Zamir White from the San Francsico 49ers for linebacker Deion Jones, ESPN reported late Sunday. Both veteran players were free agents who signed earlier this month with their teams, only to be traded. The Saints could be looking for depth with five-time Pro Bowl running back Alvin Kamara expected to miss 4-6 weeks with a sprained MCL. New Orleans signed free agent Travis Etienne to a four-year contract worth $12 million per season but head coach Kellen Moore said he envisions using a deep committee of running backs. Jones would be reunited with the 49ers' new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, his coach while both were with the Atlanta Falcons. White is listed on the 49ers "unofficial depth chart" on its website in the fourth running back group, behind starter Christian McCaffrey and four other players. White, who turns 27 on Sept. 18, played in six games last season for the Las Vegas Raiders and had 12 carries for 32 yards along with four receptions on six targets for 24 yards. Las Vegas selected White in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia. For his career, he has 198 rushing attempts for 736 yards and two touchdowns and 25 receptions for 152 yards in 45 games (nine starts) for the Raiders since 2022. He became a free agent in March and signed with the 49ers on Aug. 12. Jones, 31, played in all 17 regular-season games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season as a reserve and totaled 29 tackles. He became a free agent in March and signed with the Saints on Aug. 7. Atlanta picked Jones in the second round of the 2016 draft out of LSU. He was third in the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year that season when he intercepted three passes, returning two for scores. Jones made the Pro Bowl in his second year, when he made a career-high 138 tackles along with another three picks. For his career, Jones has 761 tackles, 12 sacks, 50 tackles for loss, 24 quarterback hits, 13 interceptions (five returned for TDs), 53 passes defended, five forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries in 128 games (91 starts) for the Falcons (2016-21), Cleveland Browns (2022), Carolina Panthers (2023) and Bucs (2024-25). Morris was a Falcons assistant coach (2015-19), defensive coordinator and interim head coach in 2020 and head coach again in 2024-25. --Field Level Media

item.title: India 419-6 at lunch after fifties by Pant, Jurel
item.description: Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel struck unbeaten fifties to push India to 419-6 at lunch on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel struck unbeaten fifties to push India to 419-6 at lunch on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday. Pant, who had retired hurt on Sunday, came out to bat after the fall of debutant Saransh Jain. Pant's 63 not out included six fours and two sixes. Asitha Fernando (4-60) dismissed Jain (six), who was caught at slip. Jurel combined with Pant in a 112-run stand for the unbroken seventh wicket to pad India's score. Jurel hit five fours in his 59 not out. India are 1-0 ahead in the two-test series.

item.title: Report: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty believed to have sprained ankle
item.description: Las Vegas running back Ashton Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle on Sunday during Raiders practice in Henderson, Nev., according to a co-report from ESPN and NFL Network late Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas running back Ashton Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle on Sunday during Raiders practice in Henderson, Nev., according to a co-report from ESPN and NFL Network late Sunday. Jeanty dove for an attempted reception on a pass route and fell awkwardly on the indoor turf surface, per multiple reports. Jeanty stayed down before being helped from the field by trainers and medical personnel. Jeanty couldn't put weight on his right leg as he left the scene. Raiders players knelt and prayed as Jeanty was assisted. The team declined comment on Jeanty's status, though it's not considered a long-term injury, per the report. Jeanty, 22, is entering his second season after the Raiders made him the No. 6 overall pick in last year's draft. He has been expected to be a major contributor for the Raiders this season. As a rookie, Jeanty ran for 975 yards with five touchdowns. He added 55 receptions for 346 yards and five touchdowns through the air. If Jeanty's injury is serious, it could mean a larger role for rookie Mike Washington Jr., who has been a star of training camp and was a fourth-round choice of the Raiders this spring. --Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Im Ringen um ein weiteres Sparpaket bei Europas größtem Autobauer Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) kritisiert die Belegschaft den Kommunikationsstil des Managements. Wegen der "desaströsen Kommunikation nach außen durch den Vorstand" seien die Mitarbeiter und ihre Familien "verunsichert und verängstigt", heißt es in einer Intranet-Meldung des Betriebsrats vom Montag, die der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters vorliegt. Der Betriebsrat habe die Stimmungslage der Belegschaft in der vergangenen Woche online abgefragt. Dabei seien auch Fragen zur Zukunft der Altersteilzeit und der Aufhebungsverträge gestellt worden, zudem sei nach Perspektiven für die Werke in Hannover, Emden, Zwickau und Neckarsulm gefragt worden. VW-Chef Oliver Blume stellt sich am Dienstag bei einer außerordentlichen Betriebsversammlung in Wolfsburg den Fragen der Mitarbeiter. Am Mittwoch sind weitere Betriebsversammlungen in Emden und Zwickau geplant. Am Freitag hatte er in einem im Intranet veröffentlichten Interview die Lage als "mehr als kritisch" bezeichnet. "3,8 Prozent operative Rendite sind in dieser anspruchsvollen Situation zwar solide", sagte Blume. "Aber sie reichen bei Weitem nicht aus, um dauerhaft ausreichende Mittel zu erwirtschaften für neue Technologien, neue Produkte und unsere Standorte." Für den Sparkurs appellierte er an die Mitarbeiter. "Auf die nächsten Wochen kommt es an: Alle müssen mitziehen. Wir haben den größten Transformationsplan in der Geschichte des Volkswagen-Konzerns aufgesetzt", sagte Blume der "Bild am Sonntag". Der Betriebsrat kritisierte, dass das interne Interview erst am Freitagnachmittag veröffentlicht worden sei, als zahlreiche Mitarbeiter bereits auf dem Weg ins Wochenende gewesen seien und zu dem Zeitpunkt die entsprechenden Informationen aus den Nachrichten erfahren hätten. Zudem habe Blume weder Details zur Zukunft der Werke in Zwickau, Emden, Hannover und Neckarsulm noch zu einem möglichen Arbeitsplatzabbau genannt. Blume hat angekündigt, die Kapazitäten in den Konzernwerken in Europa um 500.000 Fahrzeuge pro Jahr zu senken. "Für Emden, Hannover, Zwickau und Neckarsulm können wir heute keine wettbewerbsfähige Belegung für die 2030er-Jahre darstellen", sagte er. Zudem sollen die Kosten deutlich reduziert werden. Die Gemeinkosten seien um 30 Prozent höher als bei Wettbewerbern. "Die häufig genannte Zahl von rund 50.000 Stellen weltweit ist dabei keine fixe Zielgröße", sagte der VW-Chef. "Sie errechnet sich aus unserem Kostenziel im Vergleich zum Wettbewerb und gibt eine Orientierung, wie groß unser Handlungsbedarf ist."

item.title: Pro-presidential party in Kazakhstan won 71% of votes in weekend election, electoral commission says
item.description: Adilet, a newly-formed pro-government party in Kazakhstan, has won just over 71% of the vote in a parliamentary election held on Sunday, the electoral commission said on Monday, in a result likely to consolidate President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Adilet, a newly-formed pro-government party in Kazakhstan, has won just over 71% of the vote in a parliamentary election held on Sunday, the electoral commission said on Monday, in [USN:L1N44K03I TEXT:"a result likely to consolidate"] President [USN:L1N44H092 TEXT:"Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power"]. Adilet was founded in the Central Asian country earlier this year and is led by top aides to Tokayev. Shortly after its founding, it incorporated the previous ruling party, Amanat. Aside from Adilet, the electoral commission said four other blocs, the pro-business Respublika and Ak Zhol parties, the centre-left Nationwide Social Democratic Party, and the Auyl party, which represents rural voters, had entered parliament. All four opposition parties are seen as broadly supportive of Tokayev's government.

item.title: MLB roundup: Ian Happ, Pedro Ramirez slam Cubs past Mariners
item.description: Ian Happ and Pedro Ramirez hit grand slams as the Chicago Cubs poured it on late in a 19-2 shellacking of the host Seattle Mariners Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ian Happ and Pedro Ramirez hit grand slams as the Chicago Cubs poured it on late in a 19-2 shellacking of the host Seattle Mariners Sunday afternoon. Pete Crow-Armstrong and Michael Conforto also homered and right-hander Aaron Civale (6-7) pitched four innings of scoreless relief as the Cubs snapped a three-game losing streak. Chicago brought home nine runs in the eighth inning and tallied 17 hits in the beatdown. Randy Arozarena homered for the Mariners, who had won five of its previous seven games. Arozarena, who hit leadoff and walk-off homers Saturday, went deep again in the first inning Sunday to left field off Cubs starter Shota Imanaga. He became the second player to ever hit consecutive leadoff homers with a walk-off in between, duplicating Crow-Armstrong's feat from earlier in the week. Seattle starter Bryce Miller (4-8) allowed just two hits over 4 1/3 innings but was tagged for six runs due in large part to his seven walks. Imanaga lasted two-plus innings and gave up two runs (one earned) on five hits. It was the Mariners' second lopsided loss of the week, following their 22-0 road loss at Milwaukee on Tuesday. Braves 4, Brewers 2 Tyler Mahle threw five-plus solid innings to continue his impressive run and Michael Harris II homered to help Atlanta post a victory over Milwaukee in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa. Mahle (5-10) allowed one run on six hits. Mahle has a 1.52 ERA in four starts since being traded from the San Francisco Giants. Raisel Iglesias earned a four-out save for Atlanta, which had dropped five of its prior six games. Michael Harris connected on his 21st homer of the season to give Atlanta an insurance run in the top of the ninth. Milwaukee starter Shane Drohan (6-5) threw five innings and allowed two runs and eight hits for the Brewers, who had won six of their last seven. Phillies 6, Cardinals 4 Kyle Schwarber hit a two-run walk-off home run to highlight a six-run, ninth-inning rally as Philadelphia extended its winning streak to nine with a thrilling victory over visiting St. Louis. Philadelphia did not score until Edmundo Sosa's three-run double with two outs in the ninth. Bryan De La Cruz tied it with a single through the left side, and then Schwarber followed by launching a mammoth homer off the batter's eye in center field, delivering the Phillies' first walk-off homer in more than three years. Phillies star left-hander Cristopher Sanchez gave up four runs and nine hits in 6 2/3 innings. Alec Burleson knocked in a pair of runs and Jose Fermin homered for St. Louis, which concluded its season-long road trip with a 5-6 record. Kyle Leahy and four Cardinals relievers combined to blank the Phillies over the first eight innings before things fell apart for Riley O'Brien (3-5). Rays 3, Orioles 1 Tampa Bay's Nick Martinez pitched six one-hit innings and three relievers completed the task in a victory against Baltimore to avoid a series sweep. Chandler Simpson had two hits, including a run-scoring single to cap off the Rays' three-run sixth inning. Martinez (13-4) struck out four batters without issuing a walk. The only hit he allowed was Colton Cowser's one-out double in the third inning. American League-best Tampa Bay won for only the third time in their last 10 games. Cowser had both of the Orioles' hits, including a ninth-inning home run off Bryan Baker, who recorded his 37th save of the season. Shane Baz (4-14), who's winless in his last 12 starts, was charged with three runs on five hits in 5 2/3 innings against his former team. Yankees 8, Blue Jays 3 Trent Grisham worked out a two-out, bases-loaded walk to break a tie in the sixth inning, Ben Rice followed with a two-run single and New York earned a victory over visiting Toronto to claim the series. The Yankees won for the sixth time in seven games and 10th time in 15 games thanks to getting four hits in the sixth off Toronto starter Jose Soriano (10-7) and reliever Mason Fluharty. Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Grisham each added their 18th homer of the season for New York. Yankees starter Carlos Rodon allowed two runs (one earned) on two hits in four innings in his second start since returning from left elbow inflammation. The Blue Jays, who finished a 13-game stretch against AL East opponents with an 8-5 record, scored their runs on sacrifice flies by Brett Bateman and Daz Cameron and an Alejandro Kirk RBI single. Athletics 7, Astros 6 Max Muncy slugged a tiebreaking home run with two outs in the top of the seventh inning and the visiting Athletics rallied from a six-run deficit to claim the rubber match of a three-game series in Houston. Muncy crushed a 1-2 fastball from Astros reliever Steven Okert (6-2) 409 feet to center field, snapping a 6-6 deadlock. That was the deciding blow against the Astros, who dropped into a tie atop the American League West with the Texas Rangers. The Athletics trailed 6-0 entering the top of the fifth before fashioning the comeback with a six-run inning, first against Astros starter Cristian Javier before continuing it against reliever Enyel De Los Santos. The big blow was a three-run homer by No. 9 hitter Brian Serven. Marlins 6, Nationals 2 Xavier Edwards stroked a go-ahead, two-run single in the fifth inning as host Miami completed a three-game sweep with a victory over Washington. Miami improved to 8-1 against Washington this season. Marlins reliever Michael Petersen (3-3) got one out to earn the win. While the Marlins are National League wild-card contenders, the Nationals have lost 10 of their past 12 games. Nationals rookie starter Jackson Kent (0-2) took the loss, allowing three runs and four hits in 4 2/3 innings. Dodgers 4, Pirates 0 Blake Snell delivered his third consecutive strong outing in his return from an elbow procedure and Los Angeles finished off a three-game sweep over visiting Pittsburgh. Alek Thomas had an RBI single in his second game with the Dodgers and Hunter Feduccia added his own RBI single as the Dodgers extended their winning streak to six games while improving to 10-3 since Aug. 10. Snell (2-1) gave up just two hits over six scoreless innings. Brandon Lowe and Spencer Horwitz had singles for the Pirates on an otherwise ineffective day on offense. Pittsburgh right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski followed opener Lake Bachar -- who went two innings -- and gave up most of the damage: three runs allowed on five hits over three innings. Rangers 5, Angels 3 Cal Quantrill tossed six scoreless innings and Ezequiel Duran and Elias Diaz each belted a solo homer, lifting Texas to a victory over Los Angeles in the rubber match at Arlington, Texas. Quantrill (6-4) allowed six hits. He posted his second straight scoreless outing and has yielded just one run on 14 hits over his last four appearances (19 innings). Corey Seager had a pair of singles to record his sixth multi-hit performance in seven games. Yusei Kikuchi (0-4) permitted five runs on seven hits in five innings in his return from the 60-day injured list for the Angels. He had been sidelined since April with left shoulder inflammation. Los Angeles' Zach Neto went deep to lead off the eighth inning for his team-leading 22nd homer of the season. White Sox 2, Mets 1 Tristan Peters hit a walk-off homer in the ninth inning for Chicago, which edged visiting New York in the rubber game of a three-game series. Peters' one-out blast to center off Kodai Senga (0-9) glanced off the glove of a leaping A.J. Ewing for his second quirky homer in as many days. Andrew Benintendi snapped a scoreless tie with an eighth-inning RBI double for the American League Central-leading White Sox. Carson Benge and Francisco Lindor had two hits apiece for the last-place Mets, who fell to 12-6 since the trade deadline. New York starter Nolan McLean recorded another solid start by allowing one hit over six innings. Red Sox 5, Giants 4 Boston flipped a one-run deficit with three runs off three straight two-out hits in the fourth inning en route to a win over visiting San Francisco. Mickey Gasper's pinch-hit double knocked in the go-ahead run. Ceddanne Rafaela went 3-for-4 with two RBIs, and Nick Sogard doubled and homered to lead four Red Sox with multi-hit games. Jake Bennett (8-6) bounced back from a 23-pitch first inning to complete seven frames for the third time. He allowed four runs (three earned). Jonah Cox homered and both he and Bryce Eldridge went 2-for-4 for the Giants. Royals 11, Tigers 7 Nick Loftin and John Rave hit home runs as Kansas City outlasted visiting Detroit to finish off a 7-0 homestand, part of an eight-game winning streak. Loftin was 3-for-4 with four RBIs out of the leadoff spot for the Royals. The long ball by Loftin was the highlight of a five-run second for Kansas City. Rave had the big hit in the fifth, a 407-foot two-run homer, after RBI doubles by Vinnie Pasquantino and Salvador Perez. All four runs were charged to left-hander Andrew Sears, who was making his MLB debut. John Schreiber (1-3) got the Royals' last two outs of the sixth to earn the win. Sears (0-1) was the bulk pitcher on a bullpen day for Detroit, allowing five runs in four-plus innings. Guardians 7, Rockies 2 Chase DeLauter tripled twice, singled, walked and drove in two runs, helping Cleveland beat Colorado in Denver to complete a three-game sweep. Jo Adell, Steven Kwan, Austin Hedges and Angel Martinez finished with two hits apiece for the Guardians. Foster Griffin (15-4) allowed two runs on five hits in five innings to improve to 3-1 since being acquired from the Washington Nationals at the Aug. 3 trade deadline. Brett Sullivan had an RBI double for Colorado, which went 0-6 on its homestand and has been swept in three consecutive home series. Rockies starter Tomoyuki Sugano (12-7) lasted just three innings, surrendering five runs on nine hits. Padres 8, Twins 1 Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and knocked in four runs, while Jackson Merrill added a homer as host San Diego completed a three-game sweep of Minnesota for its 21st win in 28 games. Walker Buehler (8-6) allowed only four hits and a run in six innings. The Twins' Brooks Lee homered off Buehler in the fifth. The game was tied 1-1 in the bottom of the sixth when the Padres pounced on the Minnesota bullpen. With one out, Kody Funderburk (3-2) walked Luis Campusano and pinch hitter Austin Hays. Jeff Hoffman relieved and walked Xander Bogaerts to load the bases. Luis Rengifo grounded a two-run double, followed by Tatis' two-run single for a 5-1 lead. Diamondbacks 5, Reds 3 Ildemaro Vargas hit a go-ahead two-run triple in a four-run seventh inning, Corbin Carroll had two extra-base hits and an RBI, and Arizona overcame a three-run deficit to beat Cincinnati in Phoenix. Vargas and Tim Tawa had two hits apiece, and six relievers combined to throw six scoreless innings. Jonathan Loiaisiga (5-3), the third Diamondbacks reliever, pitched a scoreless seventh for the win. Reds starter Andrew Abbott (6-9) gave up seven hits and four runs in six-plus innings. Sal Stewart and Dane Myers had two hits each for Cincinnati, which has lost four of its last six. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul will nach eigenen Angaben am heutigen Montag mit seinem US-Kollegen Marco Rubio telefonieren und ihm Eindrücke seiner jüngsten Reise in die Ukraine schildern. Er wolle Rubio bitten, im Sinne der Ukraine persönlich aktiv zu werden, sagte der CDU-Politiker im Deutschlandfunk. Die US-Diplomatie sei in dieser Hinsicht bisher im Wesentlichen in den Händen der Gesandten Jared Kushner und Steve Witkoff gewesen. "Möglicherweise kann ich ihn (Rubio) selber auch veranlassen, dort noch mehr zu machen, aber wir werden auch auf anderen Wegen versuchen, jetzt Gespräche anzustoßen." Es gebe eine Reihe weiterer Länder, die "einen engeren Gesprächskontakt als praktisch alle Europäer zu Russland haben", sagte Wadephul in dem Telefoninterview während seiner Rückreise. Konkret nannte er die Türkei, viele Golfstaaten und Ägypten. Mit diesen Ländern spreche die Bundesregierung. Es sei an der Zeit, parallel zur anhaltenden Unterstützung der Ukraine auch diplomatisch einen neuen Anlauf zur Beendigung des Krieges zu nehmen. "Russland wird sich militärisch nicht in der Art und Weise durchsetzen können, wie Putin das mal geplant hat. Das ist gescheitert", so Wadephul. Er wolle diesen Herbst nutzen, um "alles zu versuchen, dass wir eine diplomatische Lösung finden können - mindestens erstmal einen Waffenstillstand." Auf den Tag genau seit viereinhalb Jahren wehrt sich die Ukraine mit westlicher Unterstützung gegen den groß angelegten russischen Angriff. Zuletzt hat die Ukraine verstärkt mit einem Mangel an Munition für Raketenabwehrsysteme zu kämpfen. Wadephul erklärte, er setze sich bei anderen Ländern für die Lieferung von Patriot-Munition ein. "Was die Bundeswehr zur Verfügung gestellt hat, das ging wirklich an die Grenze des Verantwortbaren", so Wadephul. Er habe von Ländern wie Südkorea und Griechenland in dieser Hinsicht weder Zusagen noch Absagen erhalten. Am Montag begeht die Ukraine ihren 35. Unabhängigkeitstag. Zu diesem Anlass reisen einige westliche Spitzenpolitiker nach Kiew, so der neue britische Premierminister Andy Burnham. Eine Konferenz der sogenannten Koalition der Willigen zur Unterstützung der Ukraine ist parallel teils mit Teilnahme in Präsenz und teils virtuell geplant.

item.title: Volkswagen workers criticise board's communication
item.description: Volkswagen employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers further cost cuts, according to an internal works council article seen by Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"further cost cuts"], according to an internal works council article seen by Reuters on Monday. An online survey, conducted last week by Volkswagen's Group works council, found that employees and their families were "unsettled and frightened" by the board's public communication, the article said. Employees also raised concerns about job security, the future of early-retirement and severance programmes, and prospects for Volkswagen's plants in Emden, Hanover, Neckarsulm, Osnabrueck and Zwickau. In [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"an internal company memo on Friday"], CEO Oliver Blume said four of those plants were not expected to reach competitive capacity utilisation in the 2030s, but stressed that there was no decision yet on specific plant closures. The workers criticised the lack of details on the future of these plants provided on Friday. Blume has rejected accusations of withholding information. "We continuously keep our colleagues and employee representatives informed about the status of the plans—through internal channels, but above all through direct personal dialogue," he said in July in an interview published on the company's website. Volkswagen is undergoing what is considered to be its largest-ever restructuring, possibly ranging from a further [USN:L8N42Y0CC TEXT:"50,000 job cuts"] to the [USN:L8N42Y1AR TEXT:"carve-out of some divisions"]. Blume will address employees at an extraordinary meeting in Wolfsburg on Tuesday and Thomas Schmall, head of components and a member of the management board, will speak in Braunschweig. The works council called the meetings in July after employee representatives criticised the management's communication over plans to improve the automaker's competitiveness.

item.title: Germany's Wadephul to urge Rubio to take more active role on Ukraine
item.description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul plans to speak to his U.S. counterpart, Marco Rubio, by phone on Monday to urge him to become more personally involved in diplomatic efforts related to the war in Ukraine, he told radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul plans to speak to his U.S. counterpart, Marco Rubio, by phone on Monday to urge him to become more personally involved in diplomatic efforts related to the war in Ukraine, he told radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk. Wadephul, who was recently in Ukraine, told the broadcaster that U.S. diplomacy had so far been handled largely by presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. "I may be able to encourage him (Rubio) myself to do more there," the German minister said, adding that Berlin was pursuing other channels to help restart negotiations. Germany is in contact with a number of countries, including Turkey, several Gulf states and Egypt, which maintain closer ties with Russia than most European countries, Wadephul said. Negotiations between Russia and the U.S. to bring about an end to the conflict in Ukraine have largely stalled amid the war in Iran, and the Kremlin said last week that it had no information yet on a possible next visit by Kushner and Witkoff. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov [USN:L8N44I03X TEXT:"had said"] in an interview on Friday that Russia was ready to listen to [USN:L6N43P0OE TEXT:"Rubio's new ideas"] and continue dialogue with Washington.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Energiekonzern Uniper (UN0k.DE) baut seinen Gasbezug mit einem langfristigen Liefervertrag in Norwegen aus. Uniper habe einen Vertrag mit dem norwegischen Energieriesen Equinor (EQNR.OL) unterzeichnet, teilten die Unternehmen am Montag mit. Uniper beziehe von 2027 bis 2041 jährlich mehr als 30 Terawattstunden (TWh) Erdgas. Dies entspreche grob dem Gasverbrauch von mehr als zwei Millionen Haushalten in Deutschland pro Jahr. Die Vereinbarung stärke die Versorgungssicherheit des deutschen Marktes. Equinor gehört bereits jetzt zu den wichtigsten Gaslieferanten Deutschlands. Der mehrheitlich staatlich kontrollierte Konzern hatte im Zuge der Energiekrise 2022 frühere Gasmengen Russlands teilweise ersetzt. "Mit dieser Vereinbarung stärken wir die langfristige Gasversorgung Deutschlands und vertiefen zugleich unsere Zusammenarbeit mit Equinor", sagte Uniper-Chef Michael Lewis. Gemeinsam wollten die Unternehmungen Lösungen für Erdgas mit geringeren Emissionen in Deutschland weiterentwickeln. Norwegen sei ein wichtiger Partner für die Energieversorgung Europas. Diese Vereinbarung unterstreiche die starke Nachfrage nach zuverlässigen, langfristigen Gaslieferungen aus Norwegen, erklärte Equinor-Chef Anders Opedal. Sie stärke zudem die Rolle von Equinor als verlässlicher langfristiger Energiepartner für Europa.

item.title: Taiwan indicts nine over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
item.description: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia and Super Micro , accused of illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Super Micro (SMCI.O) , accused of illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China. Semiconductor powerhouse Taiwan is the world's largest producer of advanced chips used in AI applications. Prosecutors this year investigated the suspected illegal export of servers equipped with Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export controls. Washington has imposed curbs since 2022 making it illegal for such semiconductors to be exported or sold in China. In a statement, the prosecutors in the northern port city of Keelung said the defendants, whose full names they did not state, were "fully aware" that both Nvidia and Super Micro have "rigorous internal control procedures" regarding exports. However, the defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image", they added. Neither Nvidia nor Super Micro immediately responded to requests for comment. Taiwan has tightened export controls in recent years to keep advanced technology and know-how from reaching China, which claims the democratically governed island as its own territory despite the strong objections of the island's government.

item.title: Las ventas de autos eléctricos en Europa crecen por altos precios del petróleo y subsidios
item.description: Las ventas de vehículos eléctricos se aceleraron en gran parte de Europa en julio, debido a que los elevados precios del petróleo, las ayudas y la disponibilidad de modelos más asequibles animaron a los consumidores a deshacerse de sus coches con motor de combustión, según datos facilitados a Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Nick Carey
item.content:encoded: Las ventas de vehículos eléctricos se aceleraron en gran parte de Europa en julio, debido a que los elevados precios del petróleo, las ayudas y la disponibilidad de modelos más asequibles animaron a los consumidores a deshacerse de sus coches con motor de combustión, según datos facilitados a Reuters. Las ventas de vehículos eléctricos se han disparado en toda Europa desde que comenzó la guerra en Irán en febrero y provocó un encarecimiento del precio de la gasolina. La gran pregunta para muchos en el sector del automóvil es si el interés de los consumidores se desvanecerá cuando bajen los precios del petróleo, mientras que la falta de puntos de recarga públicos sigue siendo una de las principales preocupaciones. "La gente busca formas de protegerse de la volatilidad de los precios del combustible y los vehículos eléctricos son una forma estupenda de hacerlo", dijo a Reuters Adam Wood, director general de Renault (RENA.PA) UK, en el concesionario del fabricante francés en Letchworth, a 64 kilómetros al norte de Londres. "Nos encontramos en un punto de inflexión en el que los vehículos eléctricos (…) forman parte de la corriente dominante". Hace dos años, solo el 10% de las ventas de Renault en Reino Unido correspondían a vehículos eléctricos. Por el contrario, en julio de este año los vehículos eléctricos representaron más del 50% de los pedidos de la empresa y el Renault 5 —una versión renovada del modelo más vendido de Renault, lanzado originalmente en 1972— fue el mes pasado el coche eléctrico más vendido en Reino Unido, habiendo evolucionado su forma cuadrada original hacia un diseño más curvilíneo que, según la página web de Renault, ofrece una autonomía de hasta 400 kilómetros. A finales de este año, Renault también comenzará a comercializar el Twingo eléctrico, cuyo precio de salida será inferior a 20.000 libras (26.984 dólares), sin contar una posible subvención del Gobierno británico a la que Renault espera poder optar. "NO HAY NINGUNA POSIBILIDAD DE QUE VUELVA ATRÁS" Charlotte Merrell, de 32 años, acaba de comprarse un Renault Mégane eléctrico, su primer vehículo eléctrico. Según ella, recargar en casa cuesta poco más de 1 libra, frente a las 60 libras que le costaba su anterior modelo con motor de combustión. Comprar un vehículo eléctrico fue "la mejor decisión que he tomado nunca", dijo Merrell. "No hay posibilidad de que vuelva atrás". Según datos del sector, las ventas de vehículos eléctricos en la Unión Europea aumentaron un 40,5% en el primer semestre del año, en comparación con el mismo periodo de 2025, hasta superar los 1,2 millones de coches, lo que representa el 20,7% del total de ventas. Los datos facilitados a Reuters por el grupo de investigación New Automotive y la asociación sectorial E-Mobility Europe muestran que las matriculaciones de vehículos eléctricos aumentaron un 13% interanual en julio en 16 mercados que abarcan más del 90% de las ventas de automóviles en la UE y la Asociación Europea de Libre Comercio. Esto significa que los vehículos eléctricos representaron el 25,7% de todas las ventas de turismos nuevos en esos mercados. (1 dólar = 0,7412 libras)

item.content:encoded: European Central Bank policymaker Piero Cipollone said the risk of economic stagnation and a sharp increase in inflation due to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is rather remote, in an interview with Italy's ilsussidiario.net, published on Monday. "We will of course need to monitor changes in the macroeconomic environment, but for the time being there are no signs pointing to a scenario of stagflation," he said.

item.title: Xiaomi launches new Xring chip, partners with TSMC for production, sources say
item.description: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi on Monday unveiled a new version of its in-house Xring smartphone processor, betting that deeper control over key components will help strengthen its supply chain and reduce reliance on external chip suppliers.
item.dc:creator: Che Pan, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi (1810.HK) on Monday unveiled a new version of its in-house Xring smartphone processor, betting that deeper control over key components will help strengthen its supply chain and reduce reliance on external chip suppliers. The introduction of Xring O3 comes a year after Xiaomi launched its first proprietary smartphone processor, the Xring O1, marking the latest step in the world's third-largest smartphone vendor's push to join rivals such as Apple (AAPL.O) , Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Huawei in developing its own chips. TSMC (2330.TW) will manufacture the new chip using its 3-nanometre production technology, two people familiar with the matter said. One of the sources said the chip is expected to power Xiaomi's upcoming flagship folding phone, with a shipment target of 200,000 to 300,000 units. The people declined to be identified because the plans are not public. Xiaomi and TSMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the chip's manufacturer, production technology or shipment targets. Smartphone processors, or system-on-chips (SoC), integrate computing, graphics, AI processing and imaging functions into a single component. Xiaomi's chip push reflects a broader industry trend as device makers seek to differentiate products and lessen dependence on suppliers such as Qualcomm (QCOM.O) and MediaTek (2454.TW) amid intensifying competition in premium smartphones. Xiaomi said during an earnings call last week that cumulative shipments of devices powered by the Xring O1, including smartphones, tablets and watches, had surpassed 1 million units since its launch. Xiaomi has sold about 150,000 smartphones based on the Xring O1 chip since its May 2025 launch, according to the sources.

item.title: Germany's Uniper signs 15-year gas import deal with Norway's Equinor
item.description: Germany's Uniper has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor from 2027, the companies said on Monday, strengthening Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Uniper (UN0k.DE) has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor (EQNR.OL) from 2027, the companies said on Monday, strengthening Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy. The deal, which runs until 2041, equates to nearly 3% of Germany's annual gas imports, with Norway taking Russia's place as the top supplier after Moscow ended most energy ties with the continent following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The deal marks Uniper's latest move to diversify its supply base after a recent [USN:L6N43U0J6 TEXT:"agreement"] with Canada, in an attempt to reduce the risk of shortages highlighted by the war in Iran. "This long-term agreement is an important step for the future of Europe's energy system," Uniper CEO Michael Lewis said in a statement. "With this agreement, we are strengthening Germany's long-term gas supply whilst at the same time deepening our cooperation with Equinor." The companies also said they wanted to expand their cooperation to drive forward the development of natural gas with lower emissions, highlighting the reduced carbon intensity of Norwegian gas. The firms did not provide more details about the cooperation. "This agreement highlights the strong demand for reliable, long-term gas supplies from the Norwegian continental shelf, which provide energy and industrial raw materials with lower CO2 emissions than alternative sources of gas," Equinor CEO Anders Opedal said. Sources previously [USN:L1N42A0NN TEXT:"told"] Reuters that Equinor is among the parties interested in state-owned Uniper, which Berlin is seeking to divest after bailing out the utility during Europe's energy crisis in 2022.

item.title: EU approves further €6.1 billion for Ukraine's defence
item.description: The European Commission on Monday approved a further €6.1 billion ($7.12 billion) in financial aid for Ukraine to procure new defence systems, such as air defence, missiles, ammunition and radars.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission on Monday approved a further €6.1 billion ($7.12 billion) in financial aid for Ukraine to procure new defence systems, such as air defence, missiles, ammunition and radars. The EU said this latest aid package came on top of €16 billion of previously approved procurement plans, of which €8.35 billion had already been disbursed. "As Russia intensifies its attacks, we are stepping up to help Ukraine protect its people and defend its skies. Europe stands with Ukraine and we will deliver what it needs, when it needs it," said European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in a statement. ($1 = 0.8563 euros)

item.title: Shein fashions bizarre upside-down IPO
item.description: The online retailer is targeting a $27 bln valuation at best, almost 75% below its peak. Side deals mean it’ll pay some $3.5 bln, twice the IPO proceeds, to any invested at those higher levels. Professional risk-takers ought to wear their mistakes, not be compensated for them.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Hamlin
item.content:encoded: Shein’s IPO turns the concept of capital raising upside-down. The online retailer is now hoping to raise $1.8 billion in its looming stock market debut. But at the same time it will be paying around double that to investors in its private funding rounds since 2022 to make up for its shrunken valuation. In essence, that means these professional risk-takers are being compensated for their own mistakes. That's not how public listings are supposed to work. The problem stems from the near-75% decline in the value of Shein's equity, which stood at $98 billion in early 2022. Investors in a later round, where the company's worth had fallen to $64 billion, negotiated payouts in case it plummeted further. This March, the company extended the privilege to all who had sewn money into Shein at $60 billion or higher. That means the company now has to [USN:L4N44L004 TEXT:"stump up"] $3.5 billion in cash and another $120 million in stock to these irrationally exuberant venture capitalists. Sure, Shein has long insisted during its several attempts over the years to go public that it's not doing so because it needs the money. But it's bizarre indeed, to say the least, to push ahead with an IPO that costs the company twice what it's raising. Adding to the topsy-turvy nature of Shein's capital-raising saga, some of its current shareholders are coming back for more: Boyu Capital, General Atlantic and Tiger Global are among those to sign up as cornerstone investors for the offering, which will be Hong Kong’s largest this year. Given that Shein may yet deserve a deeper discount, they may be in for more pain. That's because even a $27 billion valuation looks punchy. Assume revenue hits $36 billion this year, based on annualising the adjusted first-quarter sales number. Assume 4.5% growth in 2027 and a net margin of around 3.5%, and Shein's net profit could hit $1.4 billion. Pop that on 20 times multiple, a tad below the 24.5 times Zara-owner Inditex (ITX.MC) sports, per Visible Alpha, and the equity would be worth what Shein wants IPO investors to pay for it. But the company is grappling with the end of import duty exemptions for low-value parcels in the U.S., new fees on such shipments in Europe, and investigations in both regions – which are its two largest markets. Sales grew only 1% in the first quarter, with a 2.5% net margin, after adjusting for one-off charges. And the 20 times multiple is overly generous: Inditex and other listed fashion peers have margins closer to 10%, as well as stronger sales growth. Sure, Shein could don a nattier performance than that, but it would take time to prove that any rapid recovery were sustainable. Its messy IPO is setting the scene for a financial fashion faux pas. Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin . Online fashion retailer Shein Global will price its shares at up to HK$49.50 each according to a filing on August 24. At the upper end of the range, the company could raise HK$13.9 billion ($1.8 billion), implying a valuation of $26.8 billion. Shein will pay out as much as $2.2 billion in compensation to early investors, assuming the final offer price is at the low end of the range, and issue an additional 19.6 billion in stock, worth about $120 million. It is also paying out $1.3 billion in cash to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares, who bought in when the company was valued at $60 billion or more. Cornerstone investors led by existing shareholders Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic have subscribed for about $383 million worth of Shein shares, the prospectus showed. Tencent, Greenwoods, Taikang Life and UBS Asset Management will also take stock. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: EEUU anuncia un "Día D económico" mientras Irán amenaza con detener todas sus exportaciones de crudo
item.description: Estados Unidos amenazó a Irán con lo que calificó como "la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás organizada", mientras se preparaba para poner en marcha el lunes unas sanciones económicas dirigidas contra los socios comerciales de Irán.
item.dc:creator: Yasmine Ghania, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Estados Unidos amenazó a Irán con lo que calificó como "la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás organizada", mientras se preparaba para poner en marcha el lunes unas sanciones económicas dirigidas contra los socios comerciales de Irán. Irán, por su parte, prometió detener todas las exportaciones de petróleo del golfo Pérsico "si la guerra económica continúa". El secretario del Tesoro de EEUU, Scott Bessent, ofrecerá una rueda de prensa el lunes a las 1300 hora de Washington D.C. (1700 GMT), en medio de promesas de revelar medidas aún más severas contra un país que ha soportado sanciones económicas casi continuas desde la Revolución Islámica de 1979. "Al amanecer comienza un Día D económico: la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás lanzada contra un adversario", escribió Bessent en un artículo de opinión publicado el domingo en el Financial Times. Los países en conflicto llevan semanas sin lanzar ataques militares entre sí, pero tampoco han entablado conversaciones significativas para poner fin al conflicto, que ya dura seis meses. Miles de personas han perdido la vida, la mayoría de ellas en Irán y Líbano, desde que Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaron los ataques el 28 de febrero, lo que ha mermado gran parte de la capacidad militar convencional de Irán y le ha infligido un duro golpe económico, además de causar la muerte del líder supremo iraní, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei. Sin embargo, Irán ha conservado suficiente capacidad en materia de misiles y drones como para atacar a sus vecinos del golfo Pérsico y amenazar a los petroleros en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que ha provocado que el tráfico marítimo en esta vía navegable clave quedara prácticamente paralizado y ha ejercido presión sobre los precios mundiales del combustible. Se desconoce la situación exacta del programa nuclear iraní, que los estadounidenses y los israelíes pretenden eliminar por completo. Sin detallar medidas concretas, Bessent señaló que EEUU apuntaría contra las "naciones temerosas" que practican la "política de apaciguamiento" al relacionarse con la economía y el sistema financiero iraníes. "Harían bien en considerar las consecuencias de mantener esa actitud", escribió en el Financial Times. Irán lleva días preparándose para las sanciones, emitiendo una serie de comunicados en tono enérgico que insinúan una respuesta militar de gran envergadura. Mohsen Rezaei, secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, sugirió el domingo una represalia económica. "Si la guerra económica continúa, no se exportará ni una sola gota de petróleo, ni a través del estrecho de Ormuz ni desde ningún lugar del golfo Pérsico", escribió Rezaei en una publicación en las redes sociales. "Irán considerará la participación o el apoyo de cualquier país a la guerra económica de Estados Unidos contra el pueblo iraní como un acto de guerra". Bessent había instado previamente a China a cooperar con EEUU, señalando que, históricamente, China ha obtenido la mitad de sus importaciones de petróleo de la región del golfo Pérsico. Un portavoz de la embajada de China en Washington respondió con una declaración en la que afirmaba que "las sanciones y la presión no ayudan a resolver el problema", al tiempo que abogaba por la vía diplomática. La economía iraní ya se encontraba bajo presión debido a las sanciones internacionales antes de que los ataques de EEUU e Israel destruyeran parte de su infraestructura. Aunque Teherán sigue mostrándose desafiante en apariencia, las autoridades iraníes han advertido de que nuevas medidas económicas punitivas podrían agravar las dificultades, reavivar los disturbios y erosionar aún más la legitimidad de la República Islámica. Irán entró en la guerra con una elevada inflación, una moneda debilitada, escasez energética, sanciones y profundas debilidades estructurales, y ahora debe hacer frente a una infraestructura dañada, un comercio interrumpido, la pérdida de producción y el costo de la reconstrucción. A falta de conversaciones oficiales presenciales entre EEUU e Irán —las últimas se celebraron en junio en Suiza—, otros países, como Qatar, Pakistán y Turquía, han intentado impulsar la vía diplomática. Irán dijo que el jefe del ejército pakistaní, Asim Munir, visitará Teherán el lunes como parte de los esfuerzos por restablecer la paz y la seguridad en la región, pero dio pocos detalles. Pakistán ha estado mediando en el conflicto y una fuente del Gobierno pakistaní dijo que Munir abordaría los últimos acontecimientos, incluida la amenaza de Estados Unidos de imponer nuevas sanciones. Los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán y los ataques israelíes contra Líbano durante la guerra han causado miles de muertos y millones de desplazados. Estados Unidos informó de que 18 militares habían perdido la vida y más de 750 habían resultado heridos.

item.title: Russia's Ozon says four logistics hubs targeted by Ukrainian drones
item.description: Four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon in southern Russia were targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks, the company said on Monday, bringing the number of targeted facilities to six since August 22.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon in southern Russia were targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks, the company said on Monday, bringing the number of targeted facilities to six since August 22. Ozon said its logistics hub in Makhachkala, Dagestan, was on fire after a drone attack, while workers at warehouses in Adygeysk, in the Adygeya region, and Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, had been evacuated. "According to preliminary information, several people were injured," Ozon said in a statement, referring to the facility in Makhachkala, which had halted operations. The company also said a large fire broke out at its facility in the town of Enem in the Krasnodar region. It added that facilities in Adygeya and Stavropol were not damaged. Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on news of the attack, while shares in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%. Ozon has become Russia's second e-commerce giant, after rival Wildberries, to be targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks. Work at a logistics centre in the Samara region was halted after the first Ukrainian strike on the company's facilities on August 22.

item.title: Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at a key moment for Asia
item.description: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington.
item.dc:creator: John Geddie, Yukiko Toyoda, Ben Blanchard, Aftab Ahmed
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington. The U.S. president's abrupt decision to [USN:L1N44D05G TEXT:"cut back"] military exercises with South Korea last week, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, has reinforced fears that Trump's unpredictability could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in the region, government officials and security experts said. Japan worries it too could find itself in Trump's cross-hairs as it embarks on thorny security negotiations; Taiwan is warily watching an upcoming summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping; and India is growing less certain of its place in Washington's strategic calculus. "The decision will certainly fuel growing doubts in the region about U.S. security commitments," said Jeremy Chan, a senior analyst with political risk consultancy Eurasia Group and former U.S. diplomat in Japan and China. Trump has been frustrated by the failure of U.S. allies to support his war with Iran and made it clear that many of them must spend more on their own defence, a White House official said when asked about such concerns. Washington remains committed to working with Seoul, the official added. Enmeshed in an unpopular war with Iran, Trump is [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"eager to restart talks"] with North Korea and secure a win on the international stage, according to a person briefed on discussions between U.S. and South Korean officials. 'EXTREMELY TROUBLING' FOR TOKYO But Trump's push to meet Kim - which has so far drawn a [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"frosty response"] from Pyongyang - could backfire and embolden nuclear-armed North Korea, said Itsunori Onodera, an influential Japanese lawmaker and former defence minister. Such a prospect is "extremely troubling" for Tokyo, he said on a Fuji TV news programme last Thursday. Despite Trump's overtures, Pyongyang [USN:L1N44H09Z TEXT:"fired a volley"] of ballistic missiles off its east coast earlier that day, triggering alerts in neighbouring South Korea and Japan. What worries Japanese officials more is Trump's approach as Tokyo embarks on talks with Washington over how much it should pay towards the cost of hosting U.S. forces, America's largest overseas deployment. Japan is bracing for the possibility that Trump could, with little warning, demand a sharp hike that would be politically difficult to swallow, said a senior Japanese government official, requesting anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. Trump could also wield upcoming U.S. military exercises with Japan in October as leverage, analysts say. Officials in Washington and Tokyo said they did not expect the exercises to be curtailed, though Trump could change his mind at any point, they cautioned. The drills, known as Keen Sword, may already be smaller than their 2024 iteration because of the diversion of U.S. assets and personnel to the conflict with Iran. That shift - which recently saw America's only forward-deployed aircraft carrier in Asia, the USS George Washington, depart for the Middle East to relieve the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln - has stirred concern that U.S. deterrence against China [USN:L1N3ZR088 TEXT:"is being eroded"]. During a visit to Asia this month, Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby said working with allies to ensure combat readiness along the so-called first island chain that runs from Japan through the Philippines is a priority for Washington. TRUMP, XI AND TAIWAN Nowhere are concerns about China's growing military pressure more acute than in Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by Beijing. Trump has held up approval of a $14 billion package of arms sales to Taipei in order to maintain warm relations and a fragile trade truce with China's Xi. As Trump prepares for his latest round of summitry with Xi in Washington next month, officials in Taipei say they expect Washington will at the very least carve up the arms sales into smaller chunks to try and avoid upsetting Beijing too much. Domingo Yang of the Taiwan defence ministry's think tank, the Institute for National Defence and Security Research, says there is a distinction between Trump's rhetoric and actual U.S. behaviour, noting U.S. intelligence sharing, training and patrols with Taiwan remain substantial. A U.S. Navy aircraft [USN:L1N44J00A TEXT:"transited the Taiwan Strait"] on Friday in a move the United States described as demonstrating its "commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific." Trump's latest actions have also rocked confidence in India, where the U.S. risks squandering years of efforts to draw New Delhi closer as a counterweight to Russia and China, security analysts say. It also comes after the Pentagon's decision in June to rename its Asia military headquarters to Pacific Command from Indo-Pacific Command, a move some analysts say is a sign India is no longer as strategically important to Washington. The Pentagon denied any such shift. But Trump's steep tariffs on Indian exports and repeated claims that he had mediated an India-Pakistan ceasefire had already exasperated New Delhi. Officials there are now "very, very cautious" about committing to long-term defence deals with Washington, according to two Indian sources with knowledge of the matter. "The latest decision only reinforces President Trump's transactional view of foreign affairs and serves as a reminder that differences over specific policies, even among allies, can carry costs for the broader bilateral relationship," said Pearl Pandya, senior analyst at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, a conflict monitoring group.

item.title: US refiners face historic stress test as global crisis looms
item.description: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the Iran war. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the [USN:L8N44H1WH TEXT:"Iran war"]. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures. This has global implications. U.S. refineries’ ability to sustain today’s elevated operating rates for months, or potentially years, could mean the difference between an exceptionally tight global fuel market and a full-blown supply crisis marked by acute shortages, demand destruction and widespread economic pain. A U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran in late February triggered the closure of the [USN:L6N44E0UW TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"], [USN:L4N44I05C TEXT:"disrupting"] a fifth of global oil supply and severely hampering refining operations, particularly in Asia. Meanwhile, relentless Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries caused Moscow to suspend diesel exports in July. The result has been [USN:L6N44G0ZC TEXT:"a collapse"] in global fuel production. Global refinery throughput in July fell to 81 million barrels per day (bpd), nearly 5 million bpd, or about 6%, below the level at this point last year, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). The U.S., the world's largest crude producer and second-largest refiner after China, responded by ramping up exports of [USN:L1N41C0XB TEXT:"crude"], [USN:L1N40K11P TEXT:"gasoline, diesel and jet fuel"] to record levels, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), helping avert a truly cataclysmic supply shock. For the U.S. refining industry, the past six months have been an unprecedented bonanza. Benchmark margins for converting crude into transportation fuels have averaged more than $50 a barrel since the start of the war, more than double their 10-year average. As a result, major U.S. refiners including [USN:L4N43W0YL TEXT:"Valero"] (VLO.N) , [USN:L4N442125 TEXT:"Phillips 66"] (PSX.N) , [USN:L4N4410TR TEXT:"Marathon Petroleum"] (MPC.N) and [USN:L6N43Q18H TEXT:"Exxon Mobil"] (XOM.N) posted record or near-record second-quarter earnings. To generate those bumper profits, many companies postponed planned maintenance and kept plants running at full tilt. U.S. refinery throughput has averaged around 17 million bpd since the start of the conflict, significantly above its five-year average. The question now is how long this can last before something breaks. PARTY LIKE IT’S 1997 This period of sustained maximum production has few precedents in modern history. Over the past 11 weeks, U.S. refinery utilisation rates have hovered above 95% — a sustained level not seen in more than 25 years. In fact, refineries have only achieved such prolonged rates three times, based on EIA data going back to 1990. The closest parallels came in 1997 and 1998, when U.S. refineries recorded two separate 24-week stretches of utilisation rates above 95% — first between May and October 1997 and again between April and September 1998. In the summer of 1998, the refinery fleet exceeded 100% utilisation – the only time this has occurred in EIA records. That extraordinary performance was driven by a rare combination of low crude prices and consistently strong fuel demand, giving refiners every incentive to keep operations running flat out. A similar episode followed in 2000, when refineries operated above 95% utilisation for 13 consecutive weeks, but the conditions were markedly different. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries had introduced production cuts in 1999 that caused crude prices to nearly double by mid-2000. While this squeezed refinery profit margins, it coincided with the early stages of the China-driven commodities super-cycle, when global fuel demand skyrocketed, forcing refineries to run hard to meet it. The rally ultimately ended as crude became too expensive to sustain such high operating rates. The current episode looks quite different from any of these precedents. Today's utilisation surge is being driven not by cheap feedstock or runaway demand but by a severe shortage of refining capacity caused by war-related damage in Iran and Russia. But those episodes illustrate the risk refiners are taking. A DANGEROUS PRECIPICE Running complex refining systems at breakneck speeds for extended periods inevitably increases the risk of equipment failures, accidents and unplanned outages. Faced with soaring margins and a global fuel shortage, many U.S. refiners have deferred essential maintenance originally scheduled for the second quarter, pushing much of the work into late 2026 or even 2027. The risk is that doing this could ultimately lead to sharp, unplanned capacity losses. History offers mixed lessons. The first super-refining episode in 1997 ended relatively gradually, with utilisation easing from above 95% in mid-October to around 92% a month later before quickly rebounding. The reckoning came the following year. After the 24-week run in 1998, utilisation plunged from around 95% in late September to 86% by mid-October as several refineries were forced into emergency maintenance after months of operating at full capacity. A similar pattern emerged in 2018, when an eight-week period of utilisation above 95% was followed by a rapid drop to 89% within weeks. The 2000 rally was the notable exception, as it ended without a comparable collapse. So what’s the risk of a breakdown this time? On the one hand, the industry today has a far better understanding of the risks associated with prolonged periods of elevated utilisation. Yet today’s global refining crisis is unlike anything refiners have ever faced. Fuel inventories are being depleted, while severe damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia is likely to leave the world with reduced processing capacity for years. The risk of losing further capacity is greater than at any time in the recent past because global refining output is nearly 2 million bpd below demand, according to the IEA. That creates a dangerous dilemma. The longer refining margins remain elevated, the greater the temptation for refiners to keep running flat out. But the harder they run, the greater the risk of failures that could remove even more fuel from an already stretched market. For now, America's refiners are serving as the world's supplier of last resort. The danger is that the world has become so dependent on them that even a small disruption to their operations could tip an already fragile market into a genuine fuel crisis. item.title: US LNG exports set for endurance test as high gas prices bite
item.description: U.S. LNG producers have shipped out record volumes of the super-chilled fuel so far in 2026, but rising global natural gas prices may soon curb demand from cost-sensitive buyers.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: U.S. LNG producers have shipped out record volumes of the super-chilled fuel so far in 2026, but rising global natural gas prices may soon curb demand from cost-sensitive buyers. Key forward gas and LNG prices in Europe and Asia — which together account for over 80% of U.S. LNG shipments — have climbed to their highest in more than three years, data from LSEG shows. The ongoing U.S. and Israeli war with Iran has disrupted freight traffic in the Gulf and cut LNG flows from key exporter Qatar by over 60% from the year before, according to Kpler, opening the door to higher prices and record U.S. cargoes. However, while reduced Qatari shipments have tightened markets, exporters may soon face softer demand as high cargo costs and a seasonal slowdown in gas consumption prompt buyers to delay purchases. PRICED OUT Estimated forward prices for LNG deliveries to Asia are set to climb to above $22 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) for October, November and December delivery, according to LSEG. That compares to an average of just under $17 per MMBtu for 2026 so far, and would be the highest seen in Asia since the start of 2023 when global gas markets were reeling from Russia's invasion of Ukraine and disruptions to Russian gas flows. Given that gas consumption in Asia tends to drop after summer — as demand for cooling systems eases — gas purchases by major consumers in Japan, China and South Korea are likely to soften until utilities move to restock as winter kicks in. In Europe, gas consumers are expected to face benchmark natural gas prices in the Netherlands gas trading hub of around $21.50 to $22.50 per MMBtu over the October to December period, which would be the highest since late 2022, LSEG data shows. Those elevated prices come as Europe's gas demand shows signs of softening. Expanding renewable electricity generation is [USN:L1N44A004 TEXT:"displacing gas-fired power output"], while households and businesses are increasingly electrifying heating and other energy uses in an effort to reduce fossil fuel consumption. At the same time, European gas inventories remain well below the long-term average, meaning utilities will need to replenish stockpiles before heating demand picks up. However, recent import trends suggest buyers are in no rush to secure additional LNG at current prices. Europe imported a total of 6.2 million metric tons of LNG in July, according to Kpler, the lowest July total since 2021. That slow import pace suggests buyer concerns over fuel costs currently outweigh worries about potential supply security. EXPORTER PERSPECTIVE For U.S. LNG sellers, the prospect of a near-term lull in importer demand will not be much of a concern, especially with record tallies already recorded for the first seven months of the year. U.S. firms exported just over 73 million tons of LNG from January through July, which is up 23% from the same months in 2025, Kpler data shows. But prolonged periods of high gas prices in key target markets may accelerate electrification efforts and the shift to alternative power sources. This is especially likely in cost-sensitive markets in Asia which are also home to rapidly expanding renewables generation and strong growth in battery storage systems. High natural gas prices may also serve to discourage discretionary purchases by storage operators, who will be wary of refilling tanks while prices are high in case demand stays weak through winter and limits reselling opportunities. LNG exporters will also be mindful of planned steep increases in export volumes, with several liquefaction expansions expected in the U.S. and Canada alone before the end of the decade. Most of those planned expansion projects were greenlit on the assumption that global gas consumption will continue to expand in line with supply, in every market. But if gas prices in key regions remain high enough to curb local demand and accelerate energy transition efforts, exporters may soon face serious competition when it comes to finding willing buyers, regardless of how much they may have to sell.
