Amsterdam-based online marketplace OLX said since the Iran war began, customer enquiries for EVs had jumped across its online car marketplaces in France (84%), Romania (59%), Portugal (30%) and Poland (19%). Chinese brands known for affordable models make up a growing portion of EV listings, it said. "People are getting far more confident around this new technology," said OLX CEO Christian Gisy. In a late July poll of 1,000 users by German online marketplace Carwow, 62% of respondents said switching to an EV is the best long-term response to persistently high fuel costs. ACCELERATING THE TRANSITION In Europe, traditional automakers and Chinese rivals alike have launched a growing number of more affordable models that are also supported by subsidies. In the year through July, 29% of new cars in France were EVs. And in July alone, EVs accounted for a record 35% of new car registrations, versus 17% a year before, as the country's "social leasing" EV subsidies program for lower-income car buyers kicked in. Marie-Laure Nivot, head of automotive market analysis at research firm AAA DATA, said the program "creates an environment that accelerates the transition" to EVs. DIFFERENT TRENDS AND EV OBSTACLES It's a somewhat different picture in the U.S., where the Trump administration [USN:L1N3SJ10N TEXT:"killed"] a federal EV tax break last year. So although second-quarter EV sales rose 15% versus the first quarter, they fell more than 20% year-on-year. Cox Automotive projects U.S. EV sales will fall 23% this year versus 2025, for a market share of just 6.2%, also reflecting a lack of affordable models. A dearth of public charging remains an obstacle to EV ownership for millions of Europeans who live in apartments, an issue that needs to be addressed for sales to keep growing, Ian Henry of consultancy AutoAnalysis said. "We could be near a saturation point because there are people who might want to go electric, but can't." ($1 = 0.7412 pounds)

item.title: Titans rally from early deficit to beat Seahawks in preseason action
item.description: D'Ernest Johnson's fourth-quarter touchdown run capped off the Tennessee Titans' comeback in a 19-16 win over the Seattle Seahawks in the second preseason game for each team Sunday evening in Nashville, Tenn.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: D'Ernest Johnson's fourth-quarter touchdown run capped off the Tennessee Titans' comeback in a 19-16 win over the Seattle Seahawks in the second preseason game for each team Sunday evening in Nashville, Tenn. Johnson, a well-traveled running back who played last season for the New England Patriots, scored the Titans' only touchdown from 2 yards out with 5:45 left, giving Tennessee (2-0) its first lead of the game. It capped off the Titans' 16-0 surge over the final 45 minutes after Seattle (0-2) led 16-3 at the end of the first quarter. Veteran kicker Joey Slye made all four of his field-goal attempts for Tennessee, including a 55-yarder, to score all of the team's points before the Johnson touchdown. The Titans elected to start second-year starting quarterback Cam Ward, who completed 8 of 12 passes for a team-high 69 yards in three series. Running back Tony Pollard had just two carries for 12 yards but added one catch for a team-high 33 receiving yards. Seattle did not use starting quarterback Sam Darnold, instead relying on reserves Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe. Lock played the first half, leading three first-quarter scoring drives. He opened the scoring with a 36-yard touchdown pass to Elijah Arroyo (game-high 50 receiving yards) 3:48 into the game. Seattle rookie running back Jacardia Wright extended the lead to 13-3 with 5:43 left in the first behind a 69-yard touchdown run which buoyed his eight-carry, 81-yard rushing performance. Lock finished 12-of-14 passing for 103 yards and the touchdown. Milroe did not have the same success after halftime, completing 6 of 11 passes for 52 yards and two interceptions, which were made by Anthony Hill Jr. and Derrick Canteen, with the latter's pick ending Seattle's final possession of the game. The Seahawks, who lost veteran wide receiver Jake Bobo to a season-ending knee injury at Friday's joint practice with the Titans, were dealt more bad news in the preseason game. Rookie safety Bud Clark broke his right ankle on Seattle's first defensive play. He left the field on a cart with his leg in an air cast. Head coach Mike Macdonald said Clark will be out for "multiple months." Mason Richman, a second-year guard, was injured on the Seahawks' opening offensive drive. He left the field under his own power, but Macdonald said after the game that the team believes it's a "major injury, a long-term injury" but didn't have more specifics. Seattle selected Clark in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of TCU. The Seahawks picked Richman in the seventh round in last year's draft out of Iowa. He played as a reserve in two regular-season and one playoff game last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Father of sailor aboard USS Abraham Lincoln taken into US immigration detention
item.description: The immigrant father of a U.S. sailor on board the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, which was deployed in the Middle East during the Iran war, was taken into federal immigration detention, the sailor said in a Facebook post.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The immigrant father of a U.S. sailor on board the [USN:L6N44D05W TEXT:"USS Abraham Lincoln"] aircraft carrier, which was deployed in the Middle East during the Iran war, was taken into federal immigration detention, the sailor said in a Facebook post. U.S. Border Patrol arrested Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, originally from Nicaragua, after conducting a vehicle stop in Key West, Florida, a spokesperson of the Department of Homeland Security, of which Border Patrol is a part, separately said on Sunday. "I've been deployed for over nine months, out at sea in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country that has given me everything," Joshua Aviles, the son of the detained immigrant, said on Facebook. "I just got a call that my dad was taken by ICE," he said on Saturday, adding his father had his driver's license, social security card and work permit. "We have done everything through immigration to get his green card approved, and we are just waiting. This is heartbreaking for me. I don't know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal," the Facebook post added. The DHS said Luis Manuel Aviles Roa entered the U.S. illegally and would remain in Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention pending removal proceedings. "Having a family member in the military is not a free pass to violate our nation's laws," the DHS said. President Donald Trump says his immigration crackdown is aimed at improving domestic security. Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"racial profiling"]. The Lincoln, which left the Middle East on Saturday , did not make a port call in more than 200 days. That set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea, according to Democratic lawmakers who called for answers after sailors' families raised concerns about worsening conditions on the Lincoln.

item.title: Heat sign sharp-shooting guard Klay Thompson
item.description: The Miami Heat announced on Sunday night the signing of five-time All-Star guard Klay Thompson after the final year of his contract was bought out by the Dallas Mavericks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Miami Heat announced on Sunday night the signing of five-time All-Star guard Klay Thompson after the final year of his contract was bought out by the Dallas Mavericks. While contract terms were not announced, ESPN reported on Friday that Thompson planned to sign a two-year deal worth nearly $13 million. Thompson, 36, became a free agent after clearing waivers. The Mavs bought out Thompson, who was set to make $17.5 million this season, and placed him on waivers after he told the team he wanted to play for a contender. Dallas announced his departure Friday. A 13-year NBA veteran, Thompson won four championships with the Golden State Warriors (2015, 2017, 2018, 2022). He's a two-time All-NBA third-team honoree (2015, 2016) as well as All-Defensive second team in 2019. "Klay is one of the most iconic players to ever suit up in the NBA," Heat president Pat Riley said in a news release. "A four-time battle-tested world champion who will fit perfectly into his role as an all-around player at both ends of the court. We all talk about his shooting skill, but there is so much more he brings to the game. We are blessed that Klay chose the Heat in our quest to challenge for championships." Dallas finished 26-56 and in 12th place in the NBA's Western Conference last season, while the Heat are loading up for a deep playoff run after acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo in a July trade with the Milwaukee Bucks. Miami was 43-39 last season and 10th in the Eastern Conference. It failed to make the playoffs after being knocked out of the play-in tournament by the Charlotte Hornets. Thompson is fourth all-time with 2,899 made 3-pointers and owns a 40.9% career 3-point shooting percentage. He averaged 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 21.7 minutes while shooting 38.3% from 3-point range in 69 games (eight starts) last season with Dallas. He led the Mavericks with 202 3-pointers -- his 11th season with at least 200 from long range. For his career, Thompson has averaged 18.6 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 31.4 minutes while shooting 44.8% from the field and 85.8% from the free-throw line in 934 regular-season games (822 starts) for the Warriors (2011-19, 2021-24) and Mavericks (2024-26). He missed two seasons because of knee and Achilles injuries. He set a league record with 14 3-pointers in a single game against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 29, 2018. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian central bank likely intervenes, anchoring rupee in face of global ructions, traders say
item.description: The Indian central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Monday, five traders told Reuters, to protect the rupee against pressure arising from uncertainty over the U.S.-Iran war and corporate hedging flows.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indian central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Monday, five traders told Reuters, to protect the rupee against pressure arising from uncertainty over the U.S.-Iran war and corporate hedging flows. The rupee was little changed on the day at 95.6425 per dollar, clinging to a narrow range in early trading. State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, traders said. Traders reckon that robust inflows under policy measures to strengthen India's balance of payments have bolstered the RBI's ability to support the rupee via interventions.

item.title: Pro-Palestinian protesters sentenced over blocking Golden Gate Bridge traffic in 2024
item.description: Seven protesters who blocked traffic on the Golden Gate Bridge in a 2024 pro-Palestinian protest against Israel's assault on Gaza have been sentenced to 30 days, with credit for time already served.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Seven protesters who blocked traffic on the [USN:L1N435033 TEXT:"Golden Gate Bridge"] in a 2024 pro-Palestinian protest against Israel's assault on Gaza have been sentenced to 30 days, with credit for time already served. They were convicted in July of misdemeanor charges by a San Francisco jury that remained deadlocked on the more serious charge of felony conspiracy. Defense attorneys said demonstrators acted out of a moral responsibility to oppose the devastation from Israeli strikes on Gaza and Washington's support for its ally. San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said the protest caused a safety risk for those stuck in traffic and there should be consequences when laws are broken. "Throughout history, civil disobedience has mostly involved accepting legal consequences," Superior Court Judge Teresa Caffese was quoted as saying by KQED. "In that spirit, those who blocked the bridge and disrupted the lives of hundreds of commuters should be treated respectfully, but should also be prepared to accept the consequences of their actions." The sentences included half the time in county jail while the remaining days can be served at a work release program operated by the San Francisco Sheriff's Office. There will be four days' credit for previous time already served. The sentencing also included six months of probation, and fines and restitution of over $1,000. The defendants will remain free while the case is appealed, SFGate reported. Defense attorneys argued that protesters resorted to blocking the bridge after writing letters and appealing to congressional representatives produced no result. The jury convicted the seven protesters on misdemeanor counts including false imprisonment, obstruction of thoroughfare, unlawful assembly and in one defendant's case refusal to disperse. The jury did not reach a verdict on the most serious charge of felony conspiracy, an agreement between two or more people to commit a crime coupled with an overt act, which could have had a sentence of up to 15 years. Prosecutors said they will not retry the charges.

item.title: New Zealand to introduce bill banning social media for children under 16
item.description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said on Monday his party will introduce a bill in Parliament that seeks to ban children under 16 from using social media, proposing fines of up to 10% of a platform's global revenue for non-compliance.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose, Alasdair Pal
item.content:encoded: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said on Monday his party will introduce a bill in Parliament that seeks to ban children under 16 from using social media, proposing fines of up to 10% of a platform's global revenue for non-compliance. The bill would require social media platforms to take reasonable steps to verify users' ages, including by utilising existing account information, facial technology and digital identity documents. "We simply cannot accept the harm being done to a generation of New Zealand children," Luxon said in a statement. "Social media is exposing them to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with and it's affecting their family life, mental health, sleep and education." It was not immediately clear if the bill would garner sufficient support to pass through Parliament, with one of Luxon's coalition partners, the New Zealand First party, saying it would not support it. "We have been concerned with the proposed legislation and the direction and slippery slope that legislation like this will inevitably take our country," New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, who is also the country's foreign minister, said in a post on X. In December, Australia became the world's first country to ban social media for children under 16, blocking them from platforms including TikTok, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) YouTube and Meta's (META.O) Instagram and Facebook. That legislation had been a "colossal failure," Peters said, adding that keeping children off social media should be the responsibility of parents. "I won't pretend that it will be simple or that it will be perfect," Luxon said at an event. "We won't get every single child off social media. Some will always find ways around it, but frankly, it's just way too important not to at least try."

item.title: Typhoon Narra wreaks havoc in China, Vietnam as rains lead to floods
item.description: Floods and landslides triggered by Typhoon Narra battered northern Vietnam and China's southern region of Guangxi, as accompanying heavy rains damaged infrastructure and crops.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Floods and landslides triggered by Typhoon Narra battered northern Vietnam and China's southern region of Guangxi, as accompanying heavy rains damaged infrastructure and crops. Rising floodwaters prompted China to relocate about 54,000 people, including 8,087 moved to emergency shelters, state broadcaster CCTV said. Days of heavy rain in northern Vietnam brought by Narra killed one and displaced more than 4,300 households. Narra lingered over the Beibu Gulf, also known as the Gulf of Tonkin, but weather officials said it would not make landfall, and instead bring downpours in the north. Vietnam's mountainous provinces of Lang Son and Cao Bang received between 236 mm (9 inches) and 300 mm (12 inches) of rain in the 24 hours to Monday morning, triggering floods and landslides. Floods also affected Vietnam's Quang Ninh, home to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Ha Long Bay, inundating parts of the city and disrupting tourism, fishing and transport. The typhoon disrupted daily school and office activities, and snapped power links to nearly 55,000 families, authorities said, while destroying more than 10,000 hectares (25,000 acres) of rice and other crops. In China, the waters of 15 rivers rose beyond warning levels at monitoring stations. Brown floodwaters engulfed parts of Chongzuo city in CCTV video, submerging roads and clusters of low-rise structures. Chinese rescuers in rubber boots waded through knee-deep water, with some using boats to evacuate stranded residents. Torrential rain is forecast for Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian in downpours expected to last through Wednesday, CCTV said.

item.title: Pumas UNAM y Pachuca sacan empates de último minuto en torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Pumas UNAM y Pachuca lograron el domingo agónicos empates ante Necaxa y Atlético de San Luis, respectivamente, en el cierre de la quinta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pumas UNAM y Pachuca lograron el domingo agónicos empates ante Necaxa y Atlético de San Luis, respectivamente, en el cierre de la quinta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. El club de la Universidad Autónoma de México empató como local por 1-1, mismo marcador que sacaron los "Tuzos" de Pachuca en su visita a San Luis. En el partido disputado en el estadio Olímpico Universitario de Ciudad de México, Necaxa se adelantó a los 76 minutos con un remate de cabeza del argentino Julián Carranza en el área chica tras centro enviado por Miguel Rodríguez desde el sector izquierdo. Cuando parecía que Necaxa sacaría el triunfo como visitante, Pumas rescató la igualada a los 88 minutos por conducto del argentino Luciano Herrera, quien remató de volea en el área chica tras recibir un pase de cabeza de Guillermo Martínez. "Sabemos que somos un equipo en construcción, estamos trabajando para encontrar el funcionamiento que todavía no tenemos, sin embargo generamos ocasiones de gol contra un rival que juega bien, que ya tiene un funcionamiento, creo que fuimos por el partido y creo que merecimos ganarlo, hoy nos está faltando ese último toque a la red", dijo el director técnico de Pumas, el argentino Esteban Solari. "Somos un equipo que tenemos que mejorar un montón de cosas, no estamos contentos con nuestro rendimiento, y a partir de ahí tomar lo bueno y corregir rápido lo malo porque vienen partidos importantes", agregó. Más temprano, en el estadio Libertad Financiera de San Luis, el club local se puso en ventaja a los 83 minutos cuando Luis Nájera definió con un disparo en la entrada del área que desvió un zaguero, y que dejó sin oportunidad de reaccionar al portero Carlos Moreno, quien anotó el gol del empate para Pachuca a los 93 minutos cuando fue al área rival para rematar con la cabeza un tiro de esquina enviado desde el sector izquierdo. "Sufrimos mucho, pudimos revertirlo y ayudar al equipo de una manera inesperada, pero lo importante es que el equipo sume. El técnico me dio la confianza de ir, me acerqué al segundo palo y ahí pude sorprender un poco, un buen centro, rematé con el alma, entró y ayudamos al equipo que es lo importante", dijo Moreno en una breve entrevista publicada por Pachuca en sus redes sociales tras el partido. El sábado, Guadalajara goleó por 5-2 a Tijuana, Puebla venció por 3-2 a Santos Laguna, y Atlas ganó por 2-0 como visitante al vigente campeón Cruz Azul. El viernes, América se consolidó como el líder general del torneo tras remontar y sacar un triunfo por 2-1 en su visita a Bravos de Ciudad, Tigres UANL derrotó por 2-0 al Atlante, Toluca ganó 2-1 como visitante a Querétaro, mientras que León venció por 2-0 a Monterrey.

item.title: Shein to pay up to $3.5 billion to select pre-IPO investors around Hong Kong listing
item.description: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein will pay up to $3.5 billion to selected existing investors — almost twice the fresh capital it is seeking in an IPO — to help compensate them for a sharp slide in its valuation, its prospectus showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Selena Li
item.content:encoded: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein will pay up to $3.5 billion to selected existing investors — almost twice the fresh capital it is seeking in an IPO — to help compensate them for a sharp slide in its valuation, its prospectus showed on Monday. The investors entitled to the payments in cash and extra shares include entities linked to Boyu Capital, Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Thrive Capital, Mubadala, Brookfield and others, the filings showed. They hold Shein's late-stage funding shares — Series pre-D, Series D and Series D plus preferred — which carry protections triggered by an IPO below the prices paid in earlier funding rounds. The broader group of preferred shareholders also includes Sanabil Private Equity, Coatue, D1 Capital, DST Asia, Reliance Retail, Coppel Capital, and Claure Group. The prospectus for its listing in Hong Kong does not disclose how much each investor will receive. The payments are nearly double the up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) that [USN:L1N44K04U TEXT:"Shein aims to raise"] by selling about 280 million shares in its IPO, based on the top end of its indicated price range. Shein's proposed IPO price of HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 per share would value the company at up to about $27 billion. That is below the private valuations attached to the eligible funding rounds of $60.5 billion for the Series pre-D round in 2022, $98.2 billion for the Series D round later that year and $64 billion for the Series D plus round in 2023. Shein said it could pay up to $2.2 billion in cash under the conversion adjustment protections, assuming the IPO is priced at the bottom of the range. It will also issue 19.6 million additional shares to eligible holders at no cost. Separately, Shein also agreed to make about $1.33 billion in payments to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares. That includes about $1.1 billion, payable in three instalments by March 31, June 30 and September 30. A further estimated $230.4 million, which accrues until the IPO closes, will be paid within 15 business days after IPO completion. Shein said the payments will be funded from its own financial resources. Holders of Shein's older Series A, Series B, Series C and Series C plus preferred shares are not covered, the prospectus showed. ($1 = 7.8385 Hong Kong dollars)

item.title: Nvidia discusses Perplexity investment at $30 billion-plus valuation, The Information reports
item.description: Nvidia is in talks to invest in Perplexity as part of an equity funding round that would value the AI startup at more than $30 billion, The Information reported on Sunday, citing people with knowledge of the discussion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nvidia (NVDA.O) is in talks to invest in Perplexity as part of an equity funding round that would value the AI startup at more than $30 billion, The Information reported on Sunday, citing people with knowledge of the discussion. The funding round would increase Perplexity's valuation by more than 50% from its previous financing a year ago, according to the report. Perplexity's annualized revenue has risen to more than $750 million from less than $250 million at the start of the year, the report said. Part of the revenue growth has been driven by Perplexity Computer, a cloud-based AI agent used by professionals to automate computer-based tasks, the report added, citing people familiar with the matter. Perplexity declined to comment on the Information report, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Information reported in September last year that Perplexity had finalized a [USN:L3N3UX1PS TEXT:"$20 billion valuation"]. Earlier this year, Perplexity signed a [USN:L6N3YU1E8 TEXT:"$750 million agreement"] with Microsoft (MSFT.O) to use its Azure cloud service, according to a Bloomberg News report. Perplexity is [USN:L6N42H02Y TEXT:"planning to go public"] in 2028 regardless of how the market receives the listings of Anthropic and OpenAI, CEO Aravind Srinivas told CNBC in an interview in June. The startup's high-profile backers, along with Nvidia, include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Japan's SoftBank Group (9984.T) .

item.title: Fast fashion giant Shein valued at up to $27 billion in Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's valuation has crumpled by about 70% from a private market peak of nearly $100 billion four years ago, as it looks to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) in a Hong Kong IPO launched on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's [USN:L1N44K04U TEXT:"valuation"] has crumpled by about 70% from a private market peak of nearly $100 billion four years ago, as it looks to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) in a [USN:L1N4490O6 TEXT:"Hong Kong IPO"] launched on Monday. [USN:L1N44L00S TEXT:"Shein"] is selling 280 million shares priced between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50, [USN:L4N44L004 TEXT:"valuing"] it at close to $27 billion at the top of the range. The valuation has dropped from private fundraising rounds that valued it at $98.2 billion in 2022. Here are some comments from analysts. DICKIE WONG, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT USMART SECURITIES, HONG KONG: "Honestly, I’m not that positive on the Shein IPO. Their growth has slowed down a lot already. The big problem is the U.S. already cancelled the de minimis exemption, so those small packages under $800 now have to pay tariffs, and Trump can keep that going. On top of that, Temu is competing really hard on price and product range, and Amazon also launched Amazon Haul to fight in the same space." "I expect the subscription response to be just average. While the valuation has come down significantly, I would not recommend subscribing at this stage given the slower growth outlook and regulatory pressures. An average response would suggest investors remain selective toward large cross-border e-commerce names." MAY ZHAO, INVESTMENT DIRECTOR AT STAR RIVER SECURITIES, HONG KONG: "Shein's offering ratio is only 6.59% of its total shares, which is relatively low, and the deal also comes with a greenshoe option. The company has cut valuation for multiple times. Based on its 2025 earnings, the stock is valued at around 12 to 13 times P/E, providing some valuation support. As such, we do not expect the shares to trade below the IPO price on their debut." WEIHENG CHEN, SENIOR PARTNER AND HEAD OF GREATER CHINA, LAW FIRM WILSON SONSINI, HONG KONG: "Shein may be viewed by many investors as a boomer stock in today’s market as compared with the AI and other Gen Z stocks. Its business performance and valuation also deteriorated during the years of prolonged IPO process.” NIRGUNAN TIRUCHELVAM, HEAD OF CONSUMER AND INTERNET AT ALETHEIA CAPITAL, SINGAPORE: "It (the valuation drop) shows that the enthusiasm with which investors viewed e-commerce players such as Shein (and) the so-called myriad of baby Amazons that continue to be active, has completely shifted from the heady days of 2020-22 during the pandemic to what it is today." LORRAINE TAN, DIRECTOR OF EQUITY RESEARCH FOR ASIA, MORNINGSTAR, SINGAPORE: "The drop in Shein’s valuation largely reflects the change in prospects for the company from say 2-3 years ago when its IPO was first mooted. Firstly, the added U.S. tariffs are hurting sales and dent (the) future growth outlook; and secondly, there is increased competition - notably with PDD’s Temu. Margins have slipped as a result and the company made a quarterly loss. We believe interest in Shein by global investors has probably cooled as a result, leading to the reduced listing price." GARY TAN, PORTFOLIO MANAGER, ALLSPRING GLOBAL INVESTMENTS, SINGAPORE: "The lower valuation suggests investors increasingly view Shein as an internet platform, a sector whose multiples have compressed amid AI disruption concerns." JASON CHAN, STRATEGIST, BANK OF EAST ASIA, HONG KONG: "It's a bit late for Shein to pursue an IPO. For the past two to three years, China's domestic consumer consumption has been quite weak despite different types of incentives, and for its overseas business the tariff risk is also a big overhang, so this valuation cut is pretty reasonable. The best timing might be three to five years ago and it had already missed that." KENNY NG, STRATEGIST AT CHINA EVERBRIGHT SECURITIES INTERNATIONAL, HONG KONG: "Shein launched ... with a valuation that has fallen significantly compared to earlier years." "In my view, these challenges stem from three main areas: trade protectionism (tariffs) across different countries or regions, downward pressure on the global economy affecting consumer sentiment, and fierce competition within the industry." "I believe the fact that pre-IPO investors entered at a higher valuation than the current IPO offering price will weigh on the overall investment sentiment for Shein's ongoing bookbuilding." WINSTON MA, PROFESSOR AT NYU SCHOOL OF LAW AND FORMER NORTH AMERICA HEAD OF CHINA'S SOVEREIGN WEALTH FUND CIC: "Shein’s $27 billion valuation targets a new equilibrium. "Public investors are no longer paying for hyper-growth; they are underwriting a mature cross-border platform that must now defend its profit margins against trade tariffs, higher compliance costs, and regulatory scrutiny in both US and China. "Also on valuation, Shein is experiencing its 'Zoom moment.' Just like Zoom, Shein's COVID-era business model is now being tested by the new market, where investors have aggressively rotated into AI stack-related investments. "Robust demand would affirm Hong Kong’s role as the pragmatic listing venue for large consumer and e-commerce names that face hurdles elsewhere." KENNETH GOH, DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT, UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE: "Shein is selling equity in Hong Kong while the hyperscalers borrow in global investment grade credit. Direct crowding out is hard to argue. "Hong Kong and the mainland have seen two listings this month worth comparing. Unitree is raising about $900 million at a $9 billion valuation and says its retail tranche was more than 8,000 times covered. Shein is raising $1.77 billion with cornerstones drawn largely from its own existing shareholders." "Investors who attended the presentations said Shein leaned on operational technology without the growth story now attracting capital to AI-linked businesses. The scarce resource is willingness to underwrite something that has to be explained from scratch."

item.title: British firm offers to restart mothballed Australian manganese smelter
item.description: Natrium Redox Technologies, a green technology startup based in Britain, said on Monday it had made a firm proposal to the Tasmanian government to acquire and restart Australia's only manganese smelter, to supply global battery and electric vehicle markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Natrium Redox Technologies, a green technology startup based in Britain, said on Monday it had made a firm proposal to the Tasmanian government to acquire and restart Australia's only manganese smelter, to supply global battery and electric vehicle markets. EY Parthenon said last month the Liberty Bell Bay (LBB) Smelter would [USN:L6N43I043 TEXT:"close"] after a proposed sale fell through. The smelter, formerly owned by British industrialist Sanjeev Gupta's GFG Alliance, entered voluntary administration in March and liquidation this month after suspending operations mid-last year. "We have engaged with EY Parthenon and the Tasmanian government on this proposal for six months. We have also briefed the federal government," Natrium Redox Technologies said in a statement. "Our restart proposal seeks shared input of funds with government to the level of A$15 million ($10.75 million) for a 16-week restart period and a continuation of the existing electricity contract." In a statement, Tasmanian Business Minister Felix Ellis said potential pathways for the site had been put forward, but no transaction has been completed and no commitments were made. "EY currently controls the site as liquidator, which includes decisions about its sale," he said. EY Parthenon had no immediate comment. Natrium Redox Technologies said it planned initially to use conventional smelting techniques to restart the smelter before building a pilot plant that would use new technology to produce high-purity, low-emissions manganese powder. The process uses liquid sodium in place of coking coal to strip oxygen from manganese ore. It operates at lower temperatures than traditional smelting and does not produce carbon emissions. The new technology would add 20% to 40% to the site's production and lift the smelter up the value chain from being a conventional alloy smelter into one of the highest-value manganese operations in the world by producing battery-grade materials, the company said. "Battery grade materials sell for a far higher price than conventional alloys, securing LBB’s financial future and ensuring it remains a strategically important critical minerals asset for Australia." Its proposal would provide more than 200 jobs previously linked with the smelter, as well as secure others during construction, Natrium Redox Technologies said. It also has a proposal to reprocess a A$210 million environmental liability that has accumulated from decades of slag and waste, removing environmental liabilities from the government, it said. The company emphasised that time was of the essence because the longer furnaces are idled, the harder and more expensive a restart would become. ($1 = 1.3953 Australian dollars)

item.title: Braves edge Brewers in Little League Classic
item.description: Tyler Mahle threw five-plus solid innings to continue his impressive run and Michael Harris II homered to help the Atlanta Braves post a 4-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Mahle threw five-plus solid innings to continue his impressive run and Michael Harris II homered to help the Atlanta Braves post a 4-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa. Mahle (5-10) allowed one run on six hits while striking out four and walking two. Mahle has a 1.52 ERA in four starts since being traded from the San Francisco Giants. Raisel Iglesias earned a four-out save for Atlanta, which had dropped five of its prior six games. Milwaukee starter Shane Drohan (6-5) threw five innings and allowed two runs and eight hits. He struck out five and walked three for the Brewers, who had won six of their last seven. Iglesias allowed a leadoff single to Jackson Chourio and walked Brice Turang to begin the bottom of the ninth. After William Contreras flew out to the warning track, Iglesias began a 1-6-3 double play against Jake Bauers to secure his 27th save in 30 tries. In the top of the second, Ozzie Albies and Lane Thomas singled before Mauricio Dubon slashed a ground-rule double to give the Braves a 1-0 edge. Milwaukee tied the game in the third, as Turang singled and scored on Bauers' RBI base hit. Atlanta's Drake Baldwin doubled to begin the fourth and Thomas followed that with his second single to place runners at the corners. Drohan retired the next two batters, but Sean Murphy legged out an infield single to give the Braves a 2-1 lead. Grant Anderson spelled Drohan in the sixth and allowed Dubon's one-out walk and Austin Riley's single. After he struck out Murphy, DL Hall entered as the Brewers' second reliever of the inning. Atlanta doubled its lead as Harris' soft grounder to first was bobbled by Andrew Vaughn and allowed Dubon to score. Mahle began the bottom of the sixth, but Vaughn led off with a single and Christian Yelich reached on Matt Olson's throwing error. Didier Fuentes then entered and got Joey Ortiz to ground into a double play before Luis Lara's groundout ended the threat. Lara had replaced Garrett Mitchell, who left with a forearm contusion after being hit by a pitch in the fourth. Fuentes threw two scoreless innings in relief. Dylan Lee relieved Fuentes in the eighth and surrendered a double to Yelich and a two-out triple by Lara, cutting the Brewers' deficit to 3-2. Iglesias entered and retired Gary Sanchez to strand Lara at third. Harris connected on his 21st homer of the season to give Atlanta an insurance run in the top of the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rupee little changed, caught between elevated oil and RBI support
item.description: The Indian rupee lumbered in a thin band in early trade on Monday, hemmed in between dollar demand due to elevated oil prices and sustained market interventions by the central bank.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee lumbered in a thin band in early trade on Monday, hemmed in between dollar demand due to elevated oil prices and sustained market interventions by the central bank. The currency was at 95.6675 per dollar, little changed from its close at 95.6950 in the previous session. The rupee's trading ranges have shrunk over the last two weeks as the Reserve Bank of India has stepped up interventions to anchor it amid pressures ranging from higher oil prices to surging global bond yields. On Monday, state-run banks were spotted offering dollars yet again, traders said, most likely on behalf of the RBI. Oil prices dipped in Asia trading but held above the $90 per barrel mark as investors awaited an announcement from Washington about more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. The warring nations have not conducted military strikes against each other for weeks, but they also have not engaged in meaningful talks to end the six-month-old conflict. "Market is reluctant to short dollars given Brent above USD 90 per barrel but at the same time is not able to go long either given RBI presence around 95.80. This has limited activity and compressed intraday ranges," said Abhishek Goenka, chief executive at FX advisory firm IFA Global in Mumbai. Asian currencies were mostly rangebound while regional stocks slipped led by a 3% drop in South Korean shares. India's benchmark equity gauge, Nifty 50 (.NSEI) , was up 0.1%. Looking ahead, traders will keep their focus on oil prices while also watching the impact of maturing dollar-rupee derivative contracts later this week alongside month-end corporate flows.

item.title: Indian food safety officer shakes up Mumbai, one viral raid at a time
item.description: Tukaram Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Chaturvedi, Vibhuti Sharma, Dhwani Pandya
item.content:encoded: Tukaram Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission. As a state food safety commissioner, the 51-year-old has raided food businesses in the country's commercial capital Mumbai in an unprecedented crackdown on poor hygiene and unsafe food that has captivated the public nationwide. Mundhe has led the suspension of food permits of [USN:L4N44B0ID TEXT:"four Domino's and one Pizza Hut"] outlet in recent weeks, and has also targeted cricket clubs, hotels and well-known restaurants in over 3,000 raids since he took over as Maharashtra's food safety chief in May. When a Mumbai judge accused Mundhe of selective aggression towards private outlets and asked if court canteens were checked, his teams conducted inspections there within hours, shutting some of them which operated without licenses. "Those who try to not comply, they will face what is expected from the regulator," Mundhe said in an interview with Reuters, talking about his no-nonsense approach. "You are dealing with the lives of people." Mundhe has won widespread public admiration across India because he has tapped into deep public frustration. Even though foreign chains such as Domino's (DPZ.O) and McDonald's (MCD.N) are fast expanding, it is local eateries, roadside kiosks and small restaurants — long dogged by concerns over hygiene — that remain hugely popular. Each year since 2020, Indian food inspectors have checked more than 100,000 food samples and found roughly 20% to be unsafe, substandard or lacking proper labels, government data shows. Nearly 8,000 food business licenses have been cancelled in the last three years. "Everyone has tried to normalise this for years by saying it happens in India. It's basically bottled-up anger," said Ankur Bisen, a partner at consumer consulting firm The Knowledge Company. "I have never seen anyone like Mundhe. It's giving people hope." FINDING RATS AND EXPIRED FOOD Mundhe, who is bespectacled and sports a chevron moustache, has an unconventional operating style. He has featured in TV interviews declaring nobody dare bribe him, and that he is not afraid of administrative action despite being transferred numerous times in his 21-year career as an officer of the highly regarded Indian Administrative Service. "I get transferred every year," he said in a 2018 interview. Now, his food safety team's actions go viral daily — raids lead to detailed public statements and graphic images that show interiors of eateries and [USN:L4N44C017 TEXT:"grocery warehouses"] with stained walls, crawling cockroaches and rats, and even expired food — photos that have shocked many Indians. "It was surprising. I did not expect these many violations," Mundhe said. In Mumbai, Reuters visits last week to 25 street vendors and restaurants showed heightened fear about Mundhe's raids. One vendor has swapped artificial red dye for natural chilli in Chinese offerings, while another has started changing his frying oil three times a day and requires staff to wear gloves and head caps. Mumbai's omnipresent street food 'vada pav' — a spicy potato patty in a bun — has not escaped Mundhe's attention. In June, he prohibited use of newspapers as packaging material — often used to wrap the delicacy. Customers are noticing the change and consuming street food more confidently. Supriya Wagle, 14, is happy her favourite vada pav is now being packed in cleaner butter paper, saying that is "surely a relief". CRITICISM AMID CELEBRITY STATUS After finding lapses at some Domino's and Pizza Hut stores, Mundhe's team on Friday suspended the permit of a McDonald's outlet after finding "live pest activity (cockroaches)" and "rotting food". The three companies did not respond to Reuters queries. Mundhe's crackdown has included action against a Mumbai British-era cricket club, a 70-year-old ice cream parlour and a 110-year-old Parsi Dairy. He is facing criticism from businesses that say they should be given time to adapt, with some approaching the High Court and accusing his department of high-handedness. In one case, the judges fined his department 500,000 rupees ($5,225) for continued suspension of an eatery even though it improved its compliance. "If there are observations by the court, we take it seriously ... if there is scope for improvement, we improve," Mundhe said. At an event in New Delhi on Friday, fans clicked quick selfies with Mundhe and jostled to shake his hand. One fan told him Prime Minister Narendra Modi should give him a national role. "I don't think I'm a celebrity. I'm just a food safety commissioner," he told Reuters.

item.title: North Korea preparing further Russia troop deployments, no sign move imminent, Seoul says
item.description: North Korea and Russia have deepened military cooperation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's Defence Ministry said North Korea was continuing preparations for an additional troop deployment to Russia, but had detected no signs that such a deployment was imminent, according to a South Korean lawmaker's office. The assessment came after North Korea's [USN:L1N44G0IC TEXT:"Kim Yo Jong"], sister of leader Kim Jong Un, last week denied Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's claim that Pyongyang planned to send up to 50,000 more troops to Russia to fight for its ally. South Korea's Defence Ministry said in a statement to lawmaker Yu Yong-weon that North Korea had continued to supply Russia with weapons systems, including short-range ballistic missiles, according to Yu's office. North Korea is estimated to have supplied Russia with more than 15 million rounds of artillery ammunition, measured in 152-millimetre shell equivalents, it said. The lawmaker's office, citing a South Korean Defense Intelligence Agency assessment, said North Korean missiles used in the war may have improved in accuracy through battlefield data, alongside Russian technical advice and component support. The ministry also said the development of some North Korean ballistic missiles and multiple rocket launchers assessed as being intended for use in a conflict with South Korea was nearing completion, the lawmaker's office said. The ministry added that North Korea's Hwasong-12 intermediate-range ballistic missile, capable of reaching the U.S. territory of Guam, was being prepared for operational deployment, according to Yu's office. North Korea's intercontinental ballistic missiles have the flight capability to reach the U.S. mainland, the ministry said, but key technologies, including warhead re-entry, have not been verified because all test launches have been conducted on lofted trajectories. North Korea and Russia have deepened military cooperation since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with Pyongyang supplying artillery ammunition and missiles since 2023 and deploying troops from 2024, according to South Korean, Ukrainian and Western assessments. Moscow and Pyongyang have previously denied arms transfers.

item.title: Indian shares extend cautious trade on concerns over Iran sanctions
item.description: Indian shares were little changed in early trade on Monday, extending the cautious undertone seen over the last two weeks, ahead of details about threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran.
item.dc:creator: Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Indian shares were little changed in early trade on Monday, extending the cautious undertone seen over the last two weeks, ahead of details about threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1800 GMT on Monday, after threatening to impose "the [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"toughest sanctions"] in history" on Iran. Iran in turn vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues." India's Nifty 50 (.NSEI) rose 0.14% to 24,285.6 and the Sensex (.BSESN) added 0.19% to 77,691.65, as of 9:38 a.m. IST. The indexes shed about 0.5% last week, as investors assessed the potential implications of the Middle East conflict on inflation and bond yields. The nearly six-month-old war between the U.S. and Iran has led to a surge in energy prices globally, driving inflation fears. Brent crude futures hovered around $93 per barrel. The Nifty is likely to move within a range of 24,200 to 24,600 points in the near-term, with a breakout above 24,600 unlikely as long as there are headwinds like elevated crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions, said V.K. Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments. Eight of the 16 major sectors advanced in early trade while the broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) rose 0.5% and 0.3%, respectively. Information technology companies (.NIFTYIT) , which get a bulk of their revenue from the U.S., rose 0.8%, after a 2.6% drop last week. Investors will keep a close eye on the Federal Reserve chief's address at the Jackson Hole Symposium later this week for indications on future rate actions. Among stocks, [USN:FWN44I0IU TEXT:"Vishal Mega Mart"] (VSSL.NS) jumped 9% after re-appointing Gunender Kapur as managing director and CEO. Index provider FTSE's semi-annual review of its key indexes, effective September 21, also led to modest gains in some stocks. Cupid (CUCO.NS) , Pine Labs (PINL.NS) and Anthem Biosciences (ANTH.NS) rose between 0.5% and 2%.

item.title: Dollar trading near multi-month lows, restrained by debt nerves
item.description: A wavering dollar was pinned near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the U.S. Treasury's promise to buy back more long-dated bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the U.S. and Japan.
item.dc:creator: Tom Westbrook
item.content:encoded: A wavering dollar was pinned near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the U.S. Treasury's promise to buy back more long-dated bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the U.S. and Japan. The Canadian dollar slipped 0.3% in Asia trade, to C$1.3807 per dollar, after trade talks with the U.S. collapsed and Washington imposed [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"50% tariffs on Canadian goods"], with Canada retaliating in kind. The Australian and New Zealand dollars traded just shy of three-month highs at $0.7166 and $0.5972, respectively. The euro was comfortably above $1.16 at $1.1680, while the yen kept to the strong side of 159 per dollar. Friday data showing the strongest [USN:ZON00GDKK TEXT:"U.S. services growth"] in nearly two years in August held off dollar sellers but hardly inspired a rally. The dollar logged its largest weekly drop against bitcoin in nearly 3-1/2 years on Sunday and it has been sliding sharply on gold over [USN:L1N44H0RB TEXT:"revived fears the currency will suffer"] if the U.S. tries to hold down yields. Long-end yields have been [USN:L1N44F086 TEXT:"climbing globally"] on a combination of a solid economic growth outlook, rising inflation expectations and nerves about [USN:L6N44G17Z TEXT:"ballooning sovereign debts"]. Last week, after 30-year yields hit almost two-decade highs, the U.S. Treasury announced it would [USN:L1N44G0GD TEXT:"double buybacks"] at the long end to $4 billion per operation. The size is paltry in a market worth $32 trillion, but the interventionist signal spooked traders and hit the dollar. "By attempting to hold the price of longer-duration securities from falling, this leaves the dollar as the remaining release valve to encourage foreign inflows to finance the U.S.' current account," said analysts at Goldman Sachs in a note. Sterling was firm at $1.3650 in morning trade and the yuan , which notched an eighth straight weekly rise last week, hovered near a 3-1/2-year high at 6.7232 per dollar. SANCTIONS AND WARSH Later on Monday, at 1800 GMT, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference after threatening "[USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"the toughest sanctions in history"]" on Iran, with markets focused on whether he will target [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"China"]. Iran's foreign minister has dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation. Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday. He is also sure to face questions about Treasury's buybacks. "Any comments on the balance sheet, duration supply, or term premium could move the long end more than the data itself. That said, given Warsh’s typically restrained style, we aren’t holding our breath," said BNY strategist Geoff Yu. A Thursday appearance by Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino will also be closely watched as a prelude to next month's policy meeting. In particular, investors will be looking to see if he pushes back on a shift in market pricing to see a faster pace of hikes. "Himino may signal the BOJ is moving closer to another interest rate hike," said Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategist Joe Capurso. "However, any hawkish comments are likely to exert only modest downward pressure on USD/JPY. Developments in the U.S. bond market are a more important driver of USD/JPY."

item.title: Alibaba shares slide after $10.2 billion AI share sale offered at sharp discount
item.description: Alibaba shares slumped in Hong Kong trade after the e-commerce giant launched a share sale at a sharp discount to fund its AI ambitions, with investors focused on stock dilution and execution risks.
item.dc:creator: Kane Wu, Samuel Shen, Casey Hall
item.content:encoded: China's Alibaba (9988.HK) shares slumped in Monday Hong Kong trade after it launched a $10.2 billion share sale at a sharp discount to fund its AI ambitions, with investors focused on stock dilution and execution risks. The e-commerce and cloud computing giant said it would be offering HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) in new shares at HK$112.70 apiece — an 8.4% discount to its Friday close — to fund development of chips, AI infrastructure and models. Its Hong Kong shares were ended morning trade down 9.8% at HK$111.00. "Alibaba's DNA is in e-commerce, not advanced tech," said Yang Tingwu, vice general manager of asset manager Tongheng Investment. "No matter how much it invests in AI hardware, it will likely be outmaneuvered by competitors in tech innovation." The offering has, nevertheless, seen strong demand, receiving orders totalling $28 billion with $6 billion from long-only and sovereign investors, according to three sources with knowledge of the funding who declined to be identified as the details were confidential. About 40% of the book will be allocated to long-only and sovereign investors, two sources said. Investors include major sovereign wealth funds in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, the sources added. Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company and the third-largest globally this year after offerings of nearly $85 billion from [USN:L4N4291N6 TEXT:"Alphabet"] (GOOGL.O) and $20 billion from [USN:L6N4470KC TEXT:"Intel"] (INTC.O) . "Alibaba's placement — landing alongside massive capital raises by Alphabet and Intel in the U.S. — proves that American and Chinese tech giants are operating off the exact same strategic playbook," said Winston Ma, an adjunct professor at NYU School of Law and former head of North America for sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp. "The global sovereign investors aren't blind to U.S.-China tech friction — they are compartmentalizing it," Ma said, adding that they were more comfortable with compliance issues when investing in Chinese commercial cloud and open-weight AI plays over restricted semiconductor hardware. The biggest Chinese AI names are, however, investing only a fraction of what their U.S. counterparts are doing. Capital Group, one of the world's largest active investment managers, estimates that AI-related capital expenditure by the biggest U.S. hyperscalers — Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet, Meta (META.O) and Oracle (ORCL.N) — reached $791 billion as of July 31. That compares with $118 billion for China's ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent (0700.HK) and Baidu (9888.HK) . While Chinese firms have been on the back foot compared to U.S. rivals, particularly due to years of U.S. restrictions on access to the most advanced Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips, those constraints have pushed them to develop more efficient models and infrastructure that require less computing power and capital. The share placement comes a week after Alibaba reported [USN:L4N44H0OB TEXT:"quarterly net profit"] that fell 75% from a year earlier due primarily to AI-related spending. It said it had committed nearly half of its three-year capital expenditure of 380 billion yuan ($56.5 billion) and brought forward its projected payback on AI investment to two and a half years from three due to surging demand for AI services. ($1 = 6.7229 Chinese yuan)

item.title: Scandal-hit KPMG Australia to cut nearly 400 jobs, warns of difficult market
item.description: KPMG Australia, embroiled in scandal over the misuse of confidential client information, said on Monday it would cut about 5% of its workforce, affecting 27 partners and around 360 employees, and warned of difficult market conditions next year.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: KPMG Australia, embroiled in [USN:L1N42600F TEXT:"scandal"] over the misuse of confidential client information, said on Monday it would cut about 5% of its workforce, affecting 27 partners and around 360 employees, and warned of difficult market conditions next year. Most of the headcount reduction will take place in its consulting and business services divisions. KPMG Australia CEO John Sams, who only took the helm last month, said in a statement that the firm recognised "challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust." The firm has been under intense scrutiny from the Australian government and blue-chip clients since whistleblower allegations came to light in March that its staff used inside information to win lucrative audit contracts. It is the latest of a run of scandals in the sector and last month the Australian government said it was considering [USN:L1N43302T TEXT:"breaking up"] the Big Four accounting firms — KPMG, Deloitte, EY and PwC. KPMG Australia also said on Monday that it expected economic growth to remain subdued until at least 2028, weighing on client investment and extending decision-making timeframes. "While these conditions are likely to persist, we remain focused on what we can control," Sams said. The scandal has triggered a [USN:L4N42V03T TEXT:"leadership overhaul"], with its former CEO, audit boss and chairman, as well as senior audit partners departing. KPMG Australia's overall revenue slipped 1% to A$2.26 billion ($1.6 billion) in the year ended June 2026, as the loss of government contracts contributed to a 17% slump in consulting revenue. However, four of its five divisions posted revenue growth. Revenue rose 3% in the deal advisory and infrastructure division, 11% in both the tax and legal, and audit and assurance businesses, and 6.4% in the mid-market and private division. Average pay for equity partners fell 13% for the year in the wake of the scandal and as KPMG reviewed its cost base. KPMG Australia has agreed not to [USN:L1N42N06L TEXT:"bid"] for any new federal government work until September 30, while reviews into the firm's governance, culture, ethics and integrity are underway, the government said in June. The Big Four are currently regulated as partnerships rather than companies, which means they are not subject to supervision by Australia's corporate regulator. But that could change as part of reforms flagged by the Australian government. A [USN:L1N3752T3 TEXT:"tax leaks scandal"] at peer PwC in 2023 triggered parliamentary inquiries though most recommendations have yet to be implemented. KPMG Australia also said it would simplify parts of its structure to create more integrated teams and align more closely with its global advisory services. ($1 = 1.3943 Australian dollars)

item.title: Shares, oil slip awaiting US details of Iran sanctions
item.description: Share markets slipped in Asia on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran due later in the session, while the Canadian dollar dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Cole
item.content:encoded: Share markets slipped in Asia on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] on Iran due later in the session, while the [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"Canadian dollar"] dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour. The entire tech sector was on edge for Nvidia's (NVDA.O) results on Wednesday; investors are aware how hard it will be for the chipmaker to meet stratospheric expectations. Analysts are generally looking for quarterly revenue to almost double to around $92 billion, with full-year earnings guidance seen in a range of $103 billion to $105 billion. Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, though his well-known aversion to forward guidance could lead to disappointment. "There are several reasons to expect to be underwhelmed," said Bruce Kasman, chief economist at JPMorgan, noting that past chairs have not wanted to front-run Fed decisions at the event. "Warsh will rather likely focus on aspects of his 'regime change' agenda," Kasman added. "As the Fed has already been moving toward shrinking the balance sheet, and the committee gave the balance sheet some attention in the July minutes, that might be the most likely topic for him to expound upon." Markets imply around a 40% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates when it meets on September 16 and are fully priced for a move by December. The odds could change depending on what U.S. inflation figures show this week, with median forecasts for core inflation expected to hold at 3.3% in July. Warsh is sure to face questions about Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's surprise announcement last week of at least a doubling in bond buybacks, aimed at restraining a rise in yields that was tightening financial conditions in the economy. His efforts have had little success so far, with 30-year yields at 5.2518% , not far from the recent 19-year peak of 5.3371%. Higher yields make debt more attractive compared to equities while lifting the discount applied to future earnings, highlighting the stretched nature of some valuations. SANCTIONS AND TRADE WARS Bessent is due to hold a news conference later on Monday to outline sanctions on Iran, which has shown no sign of relinquishing its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz. Brent slipped 1.4% to $93.07 ahead of the announcement, though that followed gains of 6.6% last week. U.S. crude eased 1.6% to $85.64 a barrel. Equity markets were mostly lower, with the Nikkei (.N225) off 0.5%, having fallen almost 4% last week. Tech-heavy South Korean shares (.KS11) slid 2.8%, while Taiwan (.TWII) lost 0.5% with so much riding on Nvidia. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) eased 1.3%, while Chinese blue chips (.CSI300) fell 1.2%. The Hong Kong-listed shares of [USN:L6N44L021 TEXT:"Alibaba 9988.HK"] slid 9.5% after the Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing company launched a $10.2 billion share offer and investors worried about payback from its massive AI spending. Samsung Electronics fell over 8% after a record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of AI-fueled cash windfalls. In Europe, EURO STOXX 50 futures and DAX futures eased 0.1%, while FTSE futures were flat. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures fell 0.1% and Nasdaq futures lost 0.4%. In currency markets, the dollar added 0.2% against its Canadian counterpart to 1.3790 after Prime Minister Mark Carney said his country would respond to U.S. tariffs with levies of its own as trade talks broke down. Canada will impose tariffs on U.S. steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, along with some products that the U.S. previously targeted in Canada. The dollar was on the defensive elsewhere after having lost 0.8% last week against a basket of currencies at 96.832 . The euro held at $1.1680 after rising 0.9% last week, while the dollar was flat at 158.92 yen . The dollar has been undermined as investors fret that growing U.S. debt and policy uncertainties will erode the purchasing power of the currency, driving demand for scarcer assets including gold. The yellow metal firmed another 0.8% to $4,653 an ounce , having climbed 15% for the month so far. If it holds this gain for all of August, it would be the biggest monthly rise on record.

item.title: Samsung Electronics shares skid as record shareholder returns disappoint
item.description: Shares of Samsung Electronics fell over 8% in early trade on Monday after the company’s record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of Samsung’s AI-fueled cash windfalls and greater clarity on share buybacks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) fell over 8% in early trade on Monday after the company’s record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of Samsung’s AI-fueled cash windfalls and greater clarity on share buybacks. Samsung and rival SK Hynix (000660.KS) last week announced major shareholder return plans, following [USN:L4N4410FO TEXT:"mounting pressure"] from investors to return some of the gains from their record-breaking profits as the AI boom drives demand for chips. Samsung said on Friday this year's shareholder returns would be 90 trillion won to 110 trillion won ($65 billion to $80 billion), including 30 trillion won in cash dividends in the third quarter. While five times the previous record-high returns of 2020, analysts said the projected returns were smaller than they had anticipated and that they had expected more details on the buyback plans. Samsung said it continues to commit 50% of free cash flow accumulated over the three-year period to shareholders, under its 2024 to 2026 shareholder return policy. Rival SK Hynix (000660.KS) [USN:L1N44G07U TEXT:"said"] last week it will buy back and cancel 40 trillion won of treasury shares and allocate more than 50% of its free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027 to boost shareholder returns. SK Hynix was down 2.5%. The benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) index fell 3.1%. "Unlike SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics did not mention the possibility of raising its existing shareholder return policy, nor did it announce a plan to cancel treasury shares that could more directly contribute to the stock price increase, which is disappointing," Sohn In-joon, an analyst at Eugene Securities, said in a report. SAMSUNG'S OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE Investors had been looking for a larger share of Samsung’s capital returns to come through buybacks, which would give direct support to Samsung's stock. But share buybacks could be complicated by Samsung's ownership structure, as they could push major shareholders Samsung Life and Samsung Fire above regulatory ownership limits, forcing the affiliates to sell shares to bring their combined ownership below 10%. Therefore, Samsung's remaining funds of 60 trillion won to 80 trillion won are expected to be used mainly for dividends, with only 10 trillion won to 20 trillion won expected to be allocated to share buybacks and cancellations, Kim Soo-hyun, head of research at DS Investment & Securities, said. Samsung Life (032830.KS) and Samsung Fire (000810.KS) also slumped 9.9% and 8%, respectively. Samsung Electronics said on Friday its board will decide remaining payouts in January 2027, with cash dividends, share buybacks and share cancellations to be considered. "Big capital returns, slightly below expectations," Morgan Stanley said in a report. It said investors would need to watch out for the company’s next capital-return framework, which will take effect next year. ($1 = 1,383.7100 won)

item.title: Offices, schools closed in southern Taiwan due to torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rains across southern Taiwan forced offices and schools to close on Monday and some rail services were disrupted, though not operations at major chipmaker TSMC, with officials bracing for a typhoon to hit later in the week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Torrential rains across southern Taiwan forced offices and schools to close on Monday and some rail services were disrupted, though not operations at major chipmaker TSMC, with officials bracing for a typhoon to hit later in the week. A low-pressure system has hovered over southern Taiwan for the past few days, bringing heavy rain and causing flooding. The local governments of the two cities of Kaohsiung and Tainan, home to more than four million people, ordered offices and schools closed, as did the counties of Pingtung and Chiayi and the mountainous eastern counties of Taitung and Hualien. The Kaohsiung government said it expected cumulative rainfall over the five-day period of the low-pressure system to exceed 1.3 metres (4.3 feet), nearly half what the city typically expects in an entire year. TSMC (2330.TW) , the world's largest contract chipmaker, said in a statement that it had completed routine heavy rain preparation procedures at all its Taiwan factories, which were operating normally. TSMC has factories in both Tainan and Kaohsiung, and is building new facilities in Chiayi country. Taiwan Railway said there would be disruptions on the main east coast line and trains to and from Kaohsiung and Taitung with express services cancelled and local trains dependent on weather conditions. "If you've got nothing on, for goodness sake don't go out," Taitung county chief April Yao wrote on her Facebook page. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration said separately that Typhoon Saudel, currently heading towards Japan's southern Okinawa region, is expected to pass by the northern part of Taiwan early on Friday before reaching the eastern coast of China.

item.title: Diamondbacks rally in 7th, top Reds to keep pace in wild-card race
item.description: Ildemaro Vargas hit a go-ahead two-run triple in a four-run seventh inning, Corbin Carroll had two extra-base hits and an RBI, and the host Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a three-run deficit for a 5-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday in Phoenix.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ildemaro Vargas hit a go-ahead two-run triple in a four-run seventh inning, Corbin Carroll had two extra-base hits and an RBI, and the host Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a three-run deficit for a 5-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday in Phoenix. Vargas and Tim Tawa had two hits apiece, and six relievers combined to throw six scoreless innings in the D-backs' 39th comeback victory. They have won three of their last four. Tawa singled to lead off the seventh against Andrew Abbott (6-9). Jordan Lawlar also singled, and James McCann drew a four-pitch walk to knock out Abbott, who had given up one run in six innings. Pinch hitter Lars Nootbaar hit a slow groundout to pitcher Luis Mey that brought in Tawa, and Vargas followed with a hard grounder past second base against a drawn-in infield that rolled to the wall in right-center to drive in two. Carroll's sacrifice fly scored Vargas to make it 5-3. Sal Stewart and Dane Myers had two hits each for the Reds, who have lost four of their last six. Kevin Ginkel entered with two outs and a runner on first in the ninth and pitched around a fielding error by Vargas to get Tyler Stephenson looking for his second save of the season. Jonathan Loiaisiga (5-3), the third Arizona reliever, pitched a scoreless seventh for the win. Stewart increased his major league-leading RBI total to 98 with a run-scoring single in a three-run third off Arizona starter Mitch Bratt. Eugenio Suarez capped the rally with a two-run single for a 3-0 lead. Elly De La Cruz doubled to open the inning and scored on Stewart's opposite-field hit to right. Myers doubled to right before Suarez's single. Abbott gave up seven hits and four runs in six-plus innings. He had six strikeouts and two walks. The D-backs (69-62) kept pace with the Philadelphia Phillies (73-58) and San Diego Padres (71-60) in the race for the final two National League wild-card spots. All three clubs won Sunday. Bratt gave up five hits and three runs in three innings, with three walks and three strikeouts. Carroll tripled off the center-field fence with one out in the sixth and scored on Gabriel Moreno's sacrifice fly to make it 3-1. Carroll has 16 triples. No other major leaguer has more than seven. --Field Level Media

item.title: California expected to seek TV channel sales from Paramount-Warner, WSJ reports
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is expected to ask Paramount to divest some cable channels and commit to keeping its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. before he signs off on their merger, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is expected to ask Paramount (PSKY.O) to divest some cable channels and commit to keeping its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. (WBD.O) before he signs off on their merger, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Paramount and California state officials are [USN:L6N44J066 TEXT:"set to meet"] on Monday to discuss potential ways to settle the state's antitrust lawsuit, the report said. Lawyers from both sides met on Friday to lay out an agenda for Monday's meeting, including discussions about the cable and motion-picture businesses, the Journal reported. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery declined to comment when contacted by Reuters, while the California Attorney General's office did not respond outside regular business hours. Last month, California and 11 other states[USN:L6N43G09L TEXT:" sued to block"] Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros., alleging the deal would lessen competition in film distribution and cable television, harming theaters and pay TV distributors. Some states argued the deal would harm theaters and television distributors, raise prices for consumers and make wages less competitive for workers. Paramount has said the deal will allow it to produce more, not less, and CEO David Ellison has vowed the combined film studios would release 30 movies a year. The states have called that commitment unenforceable.

item.title: Oil falls as US prepares to unveil new Iran sanctions
item.description: Brent crude futures fell to $93.45.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan, Trixie Yap
item.content:encoded: Oil prices slipped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits ahead of an expected announcement from Washington about imposing more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures fell $1.49, or 1.6%, to $92.90 by 0649 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.32 a barrel, down $1.74, or 2%. Both contracts posted their second consecutive weekly gains last week, up more than 5%, as peace talks between the U.S. and Iran hit a stalemate, capping oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world's supply used to transit. U.S. Treasury Secretary [USN:L1N44K02A TEXT:"Scott Bessent"], who is set to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners. "Oil slipped after a two-week rally as traders awaited the US plan to economically isolate Iran due later Monday," said Saxo Bank analysts in a note. Iran has condemned U.S. plans to announce new sanctions even as President Masoud Pezeshkian called for a [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"diplomatic solution"]. "The more pragmatic members of the Iranian leadership would prefer to de-escalate but the hardliners would probably prefer to fight to the bitter end," IG markets analyst Tony Sycamore said. "I think by the end of this week we will have a good idea which side of the Iranian leadership has the upper hand." Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers [USN:L1N44I07T TEXT:"have declined"] and prices have jumped as the U.S. blockade has cut Tehran's shipments, according to trade sources. However, Iran has granted permission for a number of [USN:L1N44J01S TEXT:"Iraqi oil tankers"] to pass through the Strait of Hormuz following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday. Some analysts expect the recovery in supplies from the Middle East to take even longer than anticipated as the U.S.-Iran conflict persists. "Crude (supply) is tightening. Recent weeks have seen one of the sharpest declines in oil-on-water, whilst onshore inventories are declining as well, including in China," said Morgan Stanley analysts in a note. "A reduction in supply is driving this, most notably from the Middle East where several data sources put aggregate exports back at March/April levels," they said, slowing their assumption for a recovery in Middle East supplies. Meanwhile, fewer than 20 commodity vessels [USN:L1N44L01G TEXT:"transited"] the Strait of Hormuz at the weekend, shipping data showed on Monday, as Iranian and U.S. blockades restrict traffic through the chokepoint for energy shipments.

item.title: Fernando Tatis Jr. hits two HRs as Padres complete sweep of Twins
item.description: Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and knocked in four runs Sunday, while Jackson Merrill added a homer as the host San Diego Padres finished off a three-game sweep of the Minnesota Twins by exploding late for an 8-1 win.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Fernando Tatis Jr. homered twice and knocked in four runs Sunday, while Jackson Merrill added a homer as the host San Diego Padres finished off a three-game sweep of the Minnesota Twins by exploding late for an 8-1 win. Walker Buehler (8-6) allowed only four hits and a run in six innings while walking none and fanning four. The win was San Diego's 21st in 28 games and boosted it to 11 games over .500 for the first time since May 23. The game was tied 1-1 in the bottom of the sixth when the Padres pounced on the Minnesota bullpen. With one out, Kody Funderburk (3-2) walked Luis Campusano and pinch hitter Austin Hays. Jeff Hoffman relieved and walked Xander Bogaerts to load the bases. Luis Rengifo cashed in Campusano and Hays by grounding a two-run double down the right field line, followed by Tatis' two-run single for a 5-1 lead. It marked San Diego's third four-run inning in as many games. Merrill cracked his 21st homer with one out in the seventh, a blast that was estimated at 414 feet, and Bogaerts delivered an RBI double to make it 7-1. Tatis laced a 390-foot blast off Taylor Rogers in the eighth for his 17th homer of the year and second of the day. Twins starter Bailey Ober worked around traffic for most of his five innings but kept the Padre offense in check, except for Tatis' 396-foot rifle shot into the second deck of the Western Metal Supply building behind the left field fence in the third that opened the scoring. Ober left after 87 pitches, having allowed four hits and three walks while striking out three. San Diego stranded six runners in his time on the mound.
